meta.spec_reference: ITU-T T.81 (09/92) | ISO/IEC 10918-1, JPEG still image compression, for the marker structure, the frame and scan headers, the quantization and Huffman table segments and the entropy-coded segment; JFIF 1.02 (ISO/IEC 10918-5) for APP0; EXIF 2.2 (JEITA CP-3451) and TIFF 6.0 for APP1; ICC.1:2010 Annex B.4 for the APP2 profile embedding; Adobe DCT APP14 (Adobe TN 5116); Canon CIFF 1.0 rev 4 for the APP0 HEAPJPGM block; ITU-T T.87 for the JPEG-LS SOF55 header. Decoder behaviour was measured against libjpeg-turbo 3.x djpeg, the reference implementation of the format.

schema_extensions.name: measured_gate
schema_extensions.why: An object of {decoder, observed, conclusion} recording what a real decoder actually did when the field was set wrongly. Every tier assignment that could be argued was settled by building a JPEG by hand and running libjpeg-turbo djpeg on it rather than by reasoning from the specification. Several widely held beliefs did not survive: a missing DHT is not fatal, random entropy-coded data still produces a full image, 12-bit samples decode, and arithmetic-coded frames decode. The field records the evidence so the rewrite step can see why a tier was chosen and can re-measure if the target decoder changes.

schema_extensions.name: context_value_sets
schema_extensions.why: Two fields have several disjoint legal sets selected by parser context rather than one set. DIRENTRY.tagNumber is declared three times (lines 766, 769, 772) with three different enumerations chosen by the IFD type on the stack; APP0.App0Type is declared twice (lines 1105, 1120) with two different literals in mutually exclusive branches. A single valid_values array would either merge incompatible sets or silently drop one, so each context carries its own set with its own declaration line.

schema_extensions.name: template_parse_requirement
schema_extensions.where: constraints.<field>.template_parse_requirement, and dependency notes marked TEMPLATE QUIRK or TEMPLATE LIMITATION
schema_extensions.why: Separates rules that come from the template's own incompleteness from rules that come from the format. Four matter here: APP12's loop budget is seven bytes too generous (line 1268); APP13's is two bytes short (line 1318); JPGLS declares one component specification regardless of Nf (lines 1514-1519); and the UNKNOWN struct reads a length after every marker, including the standalone markers that have none. A rewrite must satisfy these to produce files the template can re-parse, but they are not JPEG rules and are labelled so they are not mistaken for any.

schema_extensions.name: cross_check
schema_extensions.why: A second evidence line, filled verbatim from the template like the first. Used where a constraint is established in one place and consumed in another - a marker declared inside a struct and dispatched by a case label elsewhere, or a lookahead literal spanning two adjacent fields (APP0's type and subtype form the single literal 'HEAPJPGM' tested at line 1149).

schema_extensions.name: struct_alias_convention
schema_extensions.why: This template declares each struct twice, as 'typedef struct tagSOS { ... } SOS;'. Keys use the typedef alias - SOS, SOFx, APP0, DHT, DQT, DRI, DHP, COMMENT, JPGLS, UNKNOWN, IFD, DIRENTRY, CDIR, CifDirEntry, JPGFILE - because that is the name every declaration site uses and therefore the name a generator will emit. The tag names (tagSOS, tgSOFx, tagApp0, ...) appear nowhere else and are not used as key prefixes.

schema_extensions.name: nested_field_path_convention
schema_extensions.where: keys with three components, e.g. DHP.component_param.Tq
schema_extensions.why: Named nested structs are keyed by their own name (COMPSOS.compId, COMPS.Horz, Huffmann_Table.htInfo, QuanTable.Pq, URatio.num). Anonymous nested structs have no typename, so they are keyed as ENCLOSING.instance.field - DHP.component_param.id, APP12.entry.len, APP13.block.size, CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth, IFD.URatio.num. Every such key still resolves to a real declaration in the .bt.

schema_extensions.name: tier on a diversity axis
schema_extensions.why: Eleven of the axes are Tier A fields. That is not a contradiction: the decoder pins the legal SET (sampling factors 1-4, component counts 1-10, table destinations 0-3, precisions 8 and 12), but which member of that set a file uses is a completely free choice that reshapes the decode. 'must_remain_unconstrained' on such an axis means 'emit the whole legal set, do not narrow it to the convenient member' - the same identity-versus-free-choice distinction used for GIF's DATASUBBLOCK.Size. The tier_note spells out which reading applies.

schema_extensions.name: payload_wellformedness on an unmodelled segment
schema_extensions.why: The template's catch-all branch declares opaque bytes, but for three marker values libjpeg-turbo parses them as a real segment body. The most valuable is the arithmetic frame header: the dispatch switch routes only SOF0-SOF3 to the SOFx struct, so markers 0xFFC9-0xFFCB - and with them libjpeg-turbo's entire arithmetic decoder - are reachable ONLY through this branch. Recording it as a payload rather than as free bytes is what makes that reachable.

schema_extensions.name: enum harvest from the template
schema_extensions.why: The ExifTag enumeration has 300 members, GeoTag 31 and CasioTag2 28. Rather than transcribe them by hand, they were parsed out of lines 170-495, 499-529 and 535-562 of the .bt at merge time, so the recorded sets are exact by construction and cannot drift from the template. GeoTag is declared with no explicit initialisers, so its values are the consecutive integers 0-30 in declaration order; the harvester reproduces that rule.

schema_extensions.name: unrouted_markers_note
schema_extensions.why: Records which marker values the dispatch switch does not name, because that set is what makes UNKNOWN reachable and is not derivable from any single line of the template.

meta.structure_note: A JPEG file is a flat sequence of marker segments between a mandatory SOI and an optional EOI, each segment a two-byte 0xFF-prefixed marker followed (for all but the standalone markers) by a two-byte big-endian length that includes itself. The sequence is a single pass: quantization and Huffman tables take effect where they are defined, a frame header declares the image geometry, and a scan header is followed immediately by the entropy-coded data that carries the picture. That data is this format's compressed payload and it has TWO separable contracts - a hard byte-stuffing rule that random bytes fail about half the time, and a Huffman coding rule that decides whether the decoder runs its coefficient pipeline or its error-concealment path - so unlike WAV this format very much does have payload well-formedness, and unlike PNG it has two independent ones, the scan and the Huffman table definitions the scan draws its codewords from. The format is also recursive: three separate branches embed a complete JPEG file inside a segment of another.
meta.no_length_field_note: Ten marker values are standalone in T.81 and carry no length: the eight RSTn markers, SOI, EOI and TEM (0xFF01). Every other marker segment carries one. The template models this correctly for SOI and EOI but not for RSTn or TEM, which it routes through the UNKNOWN struct and gives a spurious length - recorded as a template limitation on UNKNOWN.szSection rather than left implicit.
meta.unrouted_markers_note: The dispatch switch at lines 1545-1624 names 18 of the M_ID enumeration's 64 distinct values. The other 46 reach the UNKNOWN struct through the default case at line 1617. Measured against libjpeg-turbo, that set splits three ways: tolerated and skipped (the unhandled APPn, DNL, TEM, RSTn), parsed by a real sub-decoder (DAC 0xFFCC and the arithmetic frame headers 0xFFC9-0xFFCB), and refused outright (0xFFC5-C8, 0xFFCD-CF, and - though these ARE routed - 0xFFDE DHP and 0xFFF7 JPGLS). Note also that the enumeration declares M_JPG14 implicitly as 0xFFFE at line 161 and then M_COMM explicitly as 0xFFFE at line 162, so it has 64 distinct values rather than 65.
meta.measurement_note: Every gate in this file marked measured_gate was established empirically. A minimal 176-byte baseline JPEG was built byte by byte from the construction documented in JPGFILE.scanData, verified to decode silently in libjpeg-turbo djpeg, Pillow and ImageMagick, and then mutated one field at a time across roughly 160 probes. The Huffman code-space predicate recorded in Huffmann_Table.length was additionally checked against djpeg by exhaustive enumeration of all 624 tables with counts 0-4 at lengths 1-4, with zero disagreements.

uncovered_field_names.why: Twenty-three of the 135 distinct field names declared in the .bt carry no constraints entry. Every one falls into a category this extraction deliberately does not key, and they are named here so the coverage audit is complete rather than merely silent.

struct_instances.reason: Instances of a struct or an array of structs, not scalar fields. Each is constrained at its leaves: dirEntries through the CifDirEntry.* entries, dirEntry through the DIRENTRY.* entries, subDir and CasioIFD through IFD.* and CDIR.*, and thumbnail and CasioMakerThumbnail through the JPGFILE.* entries, since they are complete nested JPEG files. Their cardinality is recorded in structure and their recursion budgets in the nested JPGFILE rule.

typed_value_readers.reason: The thirteen typed readers that consume an EXIF directory entry's or a CIFF entry's value. They are ordinary free-form payload bytes, which the method section says not to key: nothing inspects their contents, and their sizes are derived from DIRENTRY.nComponent and CifDirEntry.sData, both of which ARE keyed, are Tier C, and appear in diversity_axes. Which reader fires is governed by DIRENTRY.dataFormat, also keyed. Keying each array would add thirteen identical 'unconstrained' entries and say nothing the dataFormat entry does not already say.

unkeyed_ciff_imagespec_members.reason: Four of the seven members of the Canon kTC_ImageSpec property. The three that a careful reader would be tempted to constrain - imageWidth, imageHeight and componentBitDepth - are keyed as Tier C entries precisely to say 'leave these alone'. These four are recorded numbers that feed no allocation and no loop bound, so under the method's rule they are ordinary free-form payload and need no entry. They are unconstrained in exactly the same way.

CifDirEntry.storage_method.tier_rationale: A 2-bit selector with four defined states that chooses between an in-heap value (offset+size follow) and an in-record value (8 inline bytes); both states are legal and each takes a different branch of the template's if/else.
CifDirEntry.storage_method.description: CIFF directory-entry storage method: 0 = value lives in the heap at oData/sData, 1 = value is the 8 bytes stored in the entry itself; 2 and 3 are reserved by the CIFF specification.

evidence.snippet: uint16 storage_method : 2; // 00 in heap, 01 in entry

CifDirEntry.storage_method.notes: The enum CIFFTagStg at lines 592-597 names all four. The template only distinguishes kStg_InHeapSpace from everything else (line 576), so 1, 2 and 3 all take the in-record branch. The two reserved states are kept because CIFF readers that do dispatch on all four take a different path for each.

CifDirEntry.data_type.tier_rationale: A 3-bit field whose seven defined states select the payload decoding branch at line 700; each value reaches a different case and a wrong value simply falls to the default case rather than failing the parse.
CifDirEntry.data_type.description: CIFF data type occupying bits 11-13 of the tag word; the template reconstructs the full CIFFTagDataType constant as data_type << 11.
CifDirEntry.data_type.notes: CIFFTagDataType (lines 599-607) defines the constants already shifted left by 11: kDT_BYTE 0x0000, kDT_ASCII 0x0800, kDT_WORD 0x1000, kDT_DWORD 0x1800, kDT_BYTE2 0x2000, kDT_HeapTypeProperty1 0x2800, kDT_HeapTypeProperty2 0x3000. Value 7 (0x3800) has no name but is representable in three bits and reaches the default branch at line 728, so it is retained. kDT_HeapTypeProperty1/2 recurse into a nested CDIR at line 726 - this is the only recursive branch in the CIFF parser and is worth reaching.

CifDirEntry.id_code.tier_rationale: An 11-bit tag identifier; the template combines it with data_type and switches on the result, and every unmatched combination falls through to a default branch, so no value can fail the parse and narrowing it would collapse the CIFF tag space to a handful of switch cases.
CifDirEntry.id_code.description: Low 11 bits of the CIFF tag word, identifying which property the entry carries.
CifDirEntry.id_code.notes: Combined as data_type << 11 | id_code at lines 580 and 687 and matched against CIFFTagType. The named constants are listed on CifDirEntry.data_type; the full 11-bit span stays legal because ReadCifDirEntry (line 653) explicitly handles the unnamed case.

CifDirEntry.sData.tier_rationale: This is the byte count the template uses to size every heap-stored value array (lines 703, 708, 713, 718, 730) and to set cDirSize for a nested directory (line 725); a value that disagrees with the bytes actually present desynchronises the heap and every subsequent entry reads from the wrong place.
CifDirEntry.sData.description: Size in bytes of this entry's value when the value is stored in the CIFF heap rather than in the entry.
CifDirEntry.sData.algorithm: byte count of the value block this entry points at
CifDirEntry.sData.covers: the bytes at cifOffset + cDirOffset-relative position oData, for sData bytes
CifDirEntry.sData.notes: For kDT_WORD the template reads sData>>1 words and for kDT_DWORD sData>>2 dwords (lines 713, 718), so sData must be a multiple of 2 and 4 respectively for the value block to be consumed exactly. Only meaningful when storage_method == kStg_InHeapSpace.

CifDirEntry.oData.tier_rationale: The template seeks to myOffset + oData at line 684 before reading the value; a wrong offset makes the parser read the wrong bytes or seek outside the segment, and the nested-directory branch at line 724 propagates the error into a recursive CDIR.
CifDirEntry.oData.description: Offset of this entry's value, measured from the start of the CIFF directory block (myOffset = cDirOffset).
CifDirEntry.oData.algorithm: byte offset from cDirOffset to the value block
CifDirEntry.oData.covers: the seek target at line 684, FSeek(myOffset + dirEntries[i].oData)
CifDirEntry.oData.notes: Values must be laid out so that the heap region [0, S) holds every value block without overlap, where S is the directory offset read back at line 671.

CifDirEntry.fileFormat.tier_rationale: An opaque Canon file-format identifier read only when the entry is kTC_ImageFormat and stored in the record; nothing compares it against anything, so every value produces a file the parser walks identically.
CifDirEntry.fileFormat.description: Canon CIFF image file format code carried inline in a kTC_ImageFormat record entry.

CifDirEntry.targetCompressionRatio.tier_rationale: A 32-bit float that no branch tests; constraining it would remove float bit patterns (denormals, NaN, infinity) that a consumer's float handling treats differently.
CifDirEntry.targetCompressionRatio.description: Canon CIFF target compression ratio carried inline in a kTC_ImageFormat record entry.

CifDirEntry.data.tier_rationale: Eight raw bytes holding an in-record value of unknown type; the template never inspects them.
CifDirEntry.data.description: Inline value bytes for a CIFF entry whose storage_method is not kStg_InHeapSpace and whose tag is not kTC_ImageFormat.

CDIR.nDirEntry.tier_rationale: The CIFF directory entry count and the bound of the dirEntries array and of both for-loops; capping it would fix how many CIFF properties a file carries and so how many times the property switch at line 687 is entered, which is exactly the repetition that reaches different cases.
CDIR.nDirEntry.description: Number of CIFF directory entries that follow; sizes dirEntries[] and bounds the loop at line 680.
CDIR.nDirEntry.notes: Total size is bounded by the output_budget on the CIFF directory structure rule, never by capping this field. Each entry is 10 bytes plus its heap value.

CDIR.szValues.tier_rationale: The template reads this same DWORD back through ReadInt(myOffset + cDirSize - 4) at line 671 and seeks to cDirOffset + S to find the entry count; if the trailing copy does not equal the real offset of nDirEntry the parser starts the directory at the wrong address and reads garbage as entry records.
CDIR.szValues.description: CIFF trailing directory offset, repeated at the end of the directory block; equals the offset from cDirOffset to the nDirEntry word.
CDIR.szValues.algorithm: byte offset from cDirOffset to the nDirEntry word (the value the template calls S)
CDIR.szValues.covers: the heap value region preceding the directory, i.e. bytes [cDirOffset, cDirOffset + S)
CDIR.szValues.notes: A CIFF directory is laid out heap-first: value blocks, then the entry count, then the entry records, then this DWORD. The template proves the round trip by seeking with the value it reads back at line 671 before it ever declares szValues.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth.tier_rationale: A recorded pixel dimension inside a Canon kTC_ImageSpec property; it sizes nothing in this template and no consumer refuses a file over it, so narrowing it would only make every generated CIFF block carry the same numbers.
CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth.description: Image width recorded in the Canon CIFF kTC_ImageSpec property.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageHeight.tier_rationale: As for imageWidth: a recorded number, not a length or a loop bound.
CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.imageHeight.description: Image height recorded in the Canon CIFF kTC_ImageSpec property.

CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.componentBitDepth.tier_rationale: A recorded bit depth that drives no allocation here; it is the kind of field a careful reader would pin to 8, which would delete every other value a CIFF-aware consumer branches on.
CDIR.DC_IMAGESPEC.componentBitDepth.description: Component bit depth recorded in the Canon CIFF kTC_ImageSpec property.

DIRENTRY.tagNumber.tier_rationale: A finite tag enumeration; the template switches on it at lines 787, 943, 962 and 1032, and several values (ExifOffset, GPSInfo, InteropOffset, MakerNote, CasioPreviewThumbnail) open whole recursive sub-parsers, so every value is a distinct branch and dropping any deletes that branch.
DIRENTRY.tagNumber.description: EXIF/TIFF, GPS or Casio tag identifier; which enumeration applies is decided by the IFD type pushed on stack_IFD_dirtype, so this one field has three disjoint legal sets.

context_value_sets.note: Used for the main IFD, the thumbnail IFD, the Exif sub-IFD (ExifOffset) and the interoperability IFD (InteropOffset).
GeoTag is declared with no explicit initialisers, so the values are the consecutive integers 0..30 in declaration order.
Only reachable when the Make field is 'CASIO COMPUTER CO.,LTD' and the Model is 'QV-R62' (lines 1052-1053).

DIRENTRY.tagNumber.notes: The five recursion-opening tags are ExifOffset 0x8769, GPSInfo 0x8825, InteropOffset 0xa005, MakerNote 0x927c and CasioPreviewThumbnail 0x2000; the last embeds a complete nested JPEG file (line 1068). Make 0x010f and Model 0x0110 are read into the CameraMake/CameraModel locals at lines 945 and 949 and gate the Casio maker-note branch. Compression 0x0103, ThumbnailOffset 0x0201, StripOffsets 0x0111, ThumbnailLength 0x0202 and StripByteCounts 0x0117 drive the APP1 thumbnail extraction at lines 1203-1213. If a tag number is not in the applicable enumeration the template still parses the entry - EnumToString simply returns an empty string - so unnamed values are legal, but the named set is what reaches the switch cases.

DIRENTRY.dataFormat.tier_rationale: Twelve defined TIFF value types, each selecting a different read at lines 876-918 and 964-1026 and a different element width from dataFormatLength; the guard at line 780 means an out-of-range value is handled rather than fatal, so this is the full legal set, not a gate.
DIRENTRY.dataFormat.description: TIFF/EXIF value type; together with nComponent it determines the length of the entry's value as dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent.

lookahead.note: Line 780 is the guard 'if (1 <= dataFormat && dataFormat < 13)'; it is not a lookahead call but it is the literal comparison a generator must satisfy to take the typed branch instead of the bare offsetData branch at line 924.

DIRENTRY.dataFormat.notes: dataFormatLength at line 744 is {0,1,1,2,4,8,1,1,2,4,8,4,8}, indexed by dataFormat, so element widths are uByte 1, ascString 1, uShort 2, uLong1 4, uRatio 8, sByte 1, undefined 1, sShort 2, sLong 4, sRatio 8, sFloat 4, dFloat 8. Values 0 and 13..65535 are legal to emit - they take the else branch at line 923 and the entry becomes a bare DWORD offsetData - but they skip the twelve typed readers, so they are worth emitting occasionally and never worth emitting exclusively. Note that the inline readers at lines 896 and 910 only fire when nComponent == 1, and sRatio and dFloat have no inline reader at all, so those combinations always take the offsetData path.

DIRENTRY.nComponent.tier_rationale: The element count of the entry's value; it multiplies with the format width to decide whether the value is inline (<= 4 bytes) or out-of-line, and it sizes eleven different arrays. Capping it would fix which side of the 4-byte boundary every entry falls on and so would silently delete either the inline branch or the offset branch.
DIRENTRY.nComponent.description: Number of elements of type dataFormat that make up this entry's value.
DIRENTRY.nComponent.notes: length = dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent (line 781). length <= 4 puts the value inline in the 4-byte value field (line 786); anything larger makes the field an offset (line 924) and the value is read at offset + offsetData in the second loop at line 961. Both branches matter. Total size is bounded by the output_budget on the IFD structure rule.

DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.tier_rationale: A closed EXIF enumeration with nine defined values; EXIF-aware consumers map each to a different label and none is refused, so the whole set is the right answer and any subset deletes labels.
DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.description: EXIF ExposureProgram value, read as a short when tagNumber is ExposureProgram and the value fits inline.

DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.tier_rationale: A closed EXIF enumeration; the 255 'other' value is deliberately far from the rest and is exactly the sort of outlier a narrowing pass would drop.
DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.description: EXIF MeteringMode value, read as a short when tagNumber is MeteringMode and the value fits inline.

DIRENTRY.LightSource.tier_rationale: A closed EXIF enumeration with two gaps (5-8 and 24-254 are undefined) and a far outlier at 255; the gaps are part of the shape and the set must be recorded as declared.
DIRENTRY.LightSource.description: EXIF LightSource value, read as a short when tagNumber is LightSource and the value fits inline.
DIRENTRY.LightSource.notes: The enum restarts explicitly at LS_Fine_weather = 9 (line 820) after LS_Flash = 4, so 5, 6, 7 and 8 are undefined; 24..254 are undefined before LS_other_light_scoure = 255.

DIRENTRY.flash_fired.tier_rationale: A single flag bit inside the EXIF Flash word; both states are legal and each is a different reading, so the bit must be free to take either value.
DIRENTRY.flash_fired.description: Bit 0 of the EXIF Flash value: whether the flash fired.
DIRENTRY.flash_fired.notes: The template splits the 16-bit Flash value into unused:9, red_eye_mode:1, flash_function:1, flash_mode:2, flash_return:2, flash_fired:1 (lines 839-844), which is 16 bits in total. Because BitfieldLeftToRight is in force (line 57) the first-declared field takes the most significant bits, so 'unused' is bits 15..7 and flash_fired is bit 0 - which matches EXIF 2.2, where the Flash tag is defined from the low bit up.

DIRENTRY.flash_return.tier_rationale: A two-bit EXIF subfield with four defined states (no strobe return detection, reserved, return light not detected, return light detected); all four are legal.
DIRENTRY.flash_return.description: Bits 1-2 of the EXIF Flash value: strobe return light status.

DIRENTRY.flash_mode.tier_rationale: A two-bit EXIF subfield with four defined states (unknown, compulsory firing, compulsory suppression, auto); all four are legal.
DIRENTRY.flash_mode.description: Bits 3-4 of the EXIF Flash value: flash mode.

DIRENTRY.flash_function.tier_rationale: A single EXIF flag bit; both states are legal.
DIRENTRY.flash_function.description: Bit 5 of the EXIF Flash value: set when the camera has no flash function.

DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.tier_rationale: A single EXIF flag bit; both states are legal.
DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.description: Bit 6 of the EXIF Flash value: red-eye reduction mode.

DIRENTRY.unused.tier_rationale: The nine high bits of the EXIF Flash word are undefined by the specification and no consumer validates them; pinning them to zero would remove the only part of this word that can carry an unexpected pattern.
DIRENTRY.unused.description: Bits 7-15 of the EXIF Flash value, undefined in EXIF 2.2.

DIRENTRY.ExposureMode.tier_rationale: A closed three-value EXIF enumeration; all three are legal.
DIRENTRY.ExposureMode.description: EXIF ExposureMode value, read as a short when tagNumber is ExposureMode and the value fits inline.

DIRENTRY.WhiteBalance.tier_rationale: A closed two-value EXIF enumeration; both are legal.
DIRENTRY.WhiteBalance.description: EXIF WhiteBalance value, read as a short when tagNumber is WhiteBalance and the value fits inline.

DIRENTRY.SceneCaptureType.tier_rationale: A closed four-value EXIF enumeration; all four are legal.
DIRENTRY.SceneCaptureType.description: EXIF SceneCaptureType value, read as a short when tagNumber is SceneCaptureType and the value fits inline.

DIRENTRY.SubjectDistanceRange.tier_rationale: A closed four-value EXIF enumeration; all four are legal.
DIRENTRY.SubjectDistanceRange.description: EXIF SubjectDistanceRange value, read as a short when tagNumber is SubjectDistanceRange and the value fits inline.

DIRENTRY.padding.tier_rationale: Filler occupying the unused part of the 4-byte value field of a short TIFF entry; TIFF 6.0 leaves its contents undefined and no reader inspects it, so pinning it to zero would remove the only unchecked bytes inside an otherwise fully determined structure.
DIRENTRY.padding.description: Bytes of the 4-byte IFD value field left over when the entry's value is shorter than 4 bytes.
DIRENTRY.padding.notes: Its length is 4 - dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent and is therefore fully determined by dataFormat and nComponent; only its contents are free. TIFF 6.0 says the value is left-justified within the 4-byte field, which is what this layout produces.

DIRENTRY.offsetData.tier_rationale: When the value does not fit in four bytes this field is the only pointer to it; the template seeks to offset + offsetData at line 961 and again at lines 1034, 1040, 1046, 1054 and 1064 to enter sub-IFDs and embedded JPEG thumbnails. A wrong offset makes every one of those reads land on unrelated bytes, and for the recursive cases it starts a nested parse at a meaningless address.
DIRENTRY.offsetData.description: Offset of this entry's value, measured from the start of the TIFF header inside APP1 (the local named offset, set at line 1180).
DIRENTRY.offsetData.algorithm: byte offset from the TIFF header origin to the value bytes
DIRENTRY.offsetData.covers: dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent bytes at offset + offsetData
DIRENTRY.offsetData.notes: Endianness follows APP1.align: big-endian for 'MM', little-endian for 'II' (line 1182). TIFF 6.0 requires the offset to be even. The same four bytes are read as ulValue by the recursion switch at lines 1034, 1040, 1046 and 1054, and as usValue at line 1204, so a generator must keep the inline and offset readings of the value field consistent with the entry's declared dataFormat.

IFD.nDirEntry.tier_rationale: The TIFF directory entry count: it sizes dirEntry[] and bounds all three loops over the directory (lines 941, 1030, 1201). Every extra entry is another pass through the dataFormat switch and another chance to hit a recursion-opening tag, so capping it directly caps how much of the EXIF parser any file can reach.
IFD.nDirEntry.description: Number of 12-byte directory entries in this IFD.
IFD.nDirEntry.notes: TIFF 6.0 puts no upper limit on the count. Size is bounded by the output_budget on the IFD structure rule, not by narrowing this field. Note that each entry is 12 bytes in the file (2 tag + 2 format + 4 count + 4 value) and may point at an arbitrarily large out-of-line value.

IFD.nextIFDoffset.tier_rationale: Zero means 'no further IFD'; any other value makes the template seek to offset + nextIFDoffset at line 1192 and parse whatever is there as a complete thumbnail IFD. A wrong non-zero value starts a full directory parse at a meaningless address, and because the thumbnail IFD is then scanned for Compression, ThumbnailOffset and ThumbnailLength it can drag an embedded JPEG parse along with it.
IFD.nextIFDoffset.description: Offset from the TIFF header origin to the next IFD in the chain, or 0 to end the chain.
IFD.nextIFDoffset.algorithm: byte offset from the TIFF header origin to the next IFD, or the sentinel 0
IFD.nextIFDoffset.covers: the IFD structure beginning at offset + nextIFDoffset
IFD.nextIFDoffset.notes: TIFF 6.0 requires the offset to be even and to point forwards. The template tests it at line 1191 and only follows a non-zero value; emitting 0 is always safe and emitting a correct forward offset is what opens the second (thumbnail) IFD and, through it, the embedded-JPEG branch at line 1222.

IFD.Header.tier_rationale: The template consumes exactly six bytes at line 1056 before parsing the maker note as an IFD; Casio Type 2 maker notes begin with the six-byte signature 'QVC' followed by three zero bytes, and a maker-note reader that does not see it does not treat the block as an IFD at all, so the nested directory is never entered.
IFD.Header.description: Casio QV-R62 maker-note header preceding the nested Casio IFD.

evidence.note: EXIF maker-note conventions (ExifTool Casio.pm, Casio Type 2): the Type 2 maker note starts with the ASCII bytes 'QVC' followed by three 0x00 bytes, after which a standard TIFF IFD follows. The template reserves exactly six bytes at line 1056 but never checks them.

IFD.Header.notes: This branch is only reachable when CameraMake begins 'CASIO COMPUTER CO.,LTD' and CameraModel begins 'QV-R62' (lines 1052-1053), which in turn requires a Make tag (0x010f) and a Model tag (0x0110) earlier in the same IFD carrying exactly those strings. Those two strings are therefore themselves Tier A for reaching this code - see the dependencies section.

IFD.URatio.num.tier_rationale: The numerator of a TIFF RATIONAL; every 32-bit value is legal and EXIF carries rationals as raw pairs.
IFD.URatio.num.description: Numerator of an unsigned rational value read out of line for a uRatio entry.

IFD.URatio.den.tier_rationale: The denominator of a TIFF RATIONAL. Zero is the tempting value to exclude because a consumer that formats the rational divides by it, but ReadURatio at line 1092 prints it without dividing and EXIF readers are expected to handle a zero denominator; excluding it would remove the one value that reaches a consumer's divide-by-zero guard.
IFD.URatio.den.description: Denominator of an unsigned rational value read out of line for a uRatio entry.
IFD.URatio.den.notes: A zero denominator is common in real files (EXIF uses 0/0 for 'unknown') and is explicitly not an error.

APP0.marker.tier_rationale: This struct is only reached from case M_APP0 of the dispatch switch at line 1569, which is selected by the two-byte lookahead at line 1544; the marker written here must equal the value that selected the branch or the file does not re-parse and the decoder resynchronises from the wrong offset.

lookahead.note: NextMarker = ReadUShort(FTell()) at line 1544 selects case M_APP0 at line 1569.

APP0.szSection.tier_rationale: Every branch of APP0 sizes its payload from this value (szSection - 2 at line 1170, szSection - 8 at lines 1125, 1135 and 1146, szSection - 2 - HeaderLength at line 1163) and the CIFF branch seeks to cifOffset + szSection - 2 at line 1166. Measured: adding or subtracting a single byte makes libjpeg-turbo resynchronise into the middle of the following segment - 'Corrupt JPEG data: 68 extraneous bytes before marker 0xc0' followed by a fatal 'Quantization table 0x00 was not defined'.
APP0.szSection.description: Length of the APP0 segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes themselves but not the two marker bytes.
APP0.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the segment payload
APP0.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment, i.e. everything after the FFE0 marker

measured_gate.observed: szSection +1 => 'Corrupt JPEG data: 68 extraneous bytes before marker 0xc0' then fatal 'Quantization table 0x00 was not defined'; szSection -1 => 'Corrupt JPEG data: 1 extraneous bytes before marker 0xdb', image still decoded
measured_gate.conclusion: A short length costs only a warning because the decoder rescans for the next marker; a long length swallows the following segment and is fatal. Both are avoided by computing the value.

APP0.szSection.notes: For the JFIF branch szSection = 2 + 5 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 3*xThumbnail*yThumbnail = 16 + 3*xThumbnail*yThumbnail. libjpeg-turbo only examines the segment as JFIF when szSection >= 16 and the first five payload bytes are 'JFIF\0'.

APP0.App0Type.tier_rationale: The five bytes are compared literally by the lookahead at line 1103 and again at line 1118; they select which of the three APP0 layouts follows. Write anything else and the template takes the 'unknown' branch at line 1170, so the entire JFIF or JFXX structure is never parsed.
APP0.App0Type.description: APP0 identifier string, either the JFIF signature or the JFIF-extension signature, each a five-byte NUL-terminated ASCII tag.

context_value_sets.context: JFIF main segment (the branch opened at line 1103)
JFIF extension segment (the branch opened at line 1118)

lookahead.note: ReadStringN wraps ReadBytes (line 99); the comparison at line 1103 selects JFIF and the one at line 1118 selects JFXX. These are exactly the literal string comparisons a generator must reproduce to enter either branch.

measured_gate.observed: Replacing 'JFIF\0' with 'XXXX\0' or 'JFXX\0': rc=0, image decoded normally
measured_gate.conclusion: libjpeg-turbo does not require APP0 to be JFIF at all - it simply does not set saw_JFIF_marker. The signature is Tier A because it gates this template's branch and every JFIF-aware consumer's density and thumbnail handling, not because the JPEG decoder refuses the file.

APP0.App0Type.notes: The field name is shared by two declarations in mutually exclusive branches; context_value_sets carries both.

APP0.versionHigh.tier_rationale: Measured: libjpeg-turbo emits 'Warning: unknown JFIF revision number 2.00' and decodes the image anyway. The value is not a gate, and emitting something other than 1 is the only way to reach that warning path, so pinning it to the JFIF-defined 1 would delete a branch rather than buy depth.
APP0.versionHigh.description: JFIF major version number, stored as the high byte of the version word.

measured_gate.observed: version 1.00, 1.01, 1.02 => rc=0 silent; version 2.00 => rc=2 'Warning: unknown JFIF revision number 2.00', image decoded; version 0.01 => rc=2 same warning, image decoded
measured_gate.conclusion: Not a gate. JFIF 1.02 defines major 1 only; every other value reaches libjpeg's JWRN_JFIF_MAJOR path.

APP0.versionHigh.notes: Declared as a bitfield 'short versionHigh:8' rather than a byte; with BitfieldLeftToRight in force this is the first (most significant) byte of the 16-bit version word, which matches JFIF's major-then-minor layout.

APP0.versionLow.tier_rationale: The JFIF minor version; libjpeg records it and never tests it. Narrowing it to the three released revisions would remove every value a stricter JFIF consumer treats as unknown.
APP0.versionLow.description: JFIF minor version number, stored as the low byte of the version word.
APP0.versionLow.notes: JFIF revisions in the wild are 1.00, 1.01 and 1.02; the field is a plain byte and no value is rejected.

APP0.units.tier_rationale: A closed three-value JFIF enumeration that selects how Xdensity and Ydensity are interpreted; a consumer that converts resolution branches on all three. Measured as not a gate, so it is Tier B rather than Tier A, and all three values belong in the set.
APP0.units.description: JFIF density unit: 0 = no units (pixel aspect ratio only), 1 = pixels per inch, 2 = pixels per centimetre.

measured_gate.observed: units 0, 1, 2, 3 and 255 all rc=0 with the image decoded
measured_gate.conclusion: libjpeg stores density_unit without validating it; values above 2 are undefined by JFIF but harmless. The three defined values are recorded as the legal set.

APP0.Xdensity.tier_rationale: A recorded resolution, not a length or a count. Measured free across the whole 16-bit span including 0. It is a classic field to pin to 72 or 300, which would make every generated file report the same resolution and would never be tested by the decoder.
APP0.Xdensity.description: JFIF horizontal pixel density, in the unit given by APP0.units.

measured_gate.observed: density 0x0, 1x1, 72x72 and 65535x65535 all rc=0
measured_gate.conclusion: Entirely free. JFIF says the density should be non-zero but libjpeg does not enforce it.

APP0.Ydensity.tier_rationale: As for Xdensity: recorded, never validated, and a prime candidate for a needless pin.
APP0.Ydensity.description: JFIF vertical pixel density, in the unit given by APP0.units.

APP0.xThumbnail.tier_rationale: This is the JPEG analogue of the GIF dimension mistake. It is a dimension, and the RGB thumbnail array at line 1116 is sized xThumbnail * yThumbnail from it. The payload must be derived from this value; the value must never be shrunk so that a fixed payload fits.
APP0.xThumbnail.description: Width in pixels of the uncompressed RGB thumbnail carried in the JFIF APP0 segment; 0 means no thumbnail.

measured_gate.observed: thumbnail 0x0, 1x1 and 4x4 with matching payload all rc=0
measured_gate.conclusion: Free across the full byte range as long as the RGB array and szSection are computed from it.

APP0.xThumbnail.notes: The array is only emitted when both xThumbnail and yThumbnail are non-zero (line 1113). szSection must be 16 + 3*xThumbnail*yThumbnail. Because the field is a ubyte the largest thumbnail is 255x255 = 195075 bytes of RGB, which is why the APP0 structure rule carries an output_budget rather than this field carrying a cap.

APP0.yThumbnail.tier_rationale: The second half of the same dimension pair; the same rule applies - derive the RGB array from it, never the reverse.
APP0.yThumbnail.description: Height in pixels of the uncompressed RGB thumbnail carried in the JFIF APP0 segment; 0 means no thumbnail.
APP0.yThumbnail.notes: Note the cast at line 1116: (ushort)xThumbnail * yThumbnail. Without it the product of two ubytes would be computed in a narrower type; the template author added the cast deliberately, which confirms the full 255x255 product is intended to be reachable.

APP0.extension_code.tier_rationale: A closed JFIF-extension enumeration selecting three completely different thumbnail encodings at lines 1123, 1129 and 1137; one of them (0x10) recurses into a whole nested JPEG file. Every value is a different structure, and an unmatched value takes the default branch rather than failing, so this is the full legal set and not a gate.
APP0.extension_code.description: JFIF extension code identifying the thumbnail format in a JFXX APP0 segment.
APP0.extension_code.notes: 0x10 embeds a complete JPEG datastream, parsed recursively as a JPGFILE with JpegFileEnd temporarily set to FTell() + szSection - 8 (lines 1124-1127) - the richest branch in the whole APP0 structure. 0x11 is a palettised thumbnail with a fixed 256-entry palette. 0x13 is raw RGB. The values are 0x10, 0x11 and 0x13; 0x12 is not defined by JFIF and reaches the default branch at line 1144.

APP0.palette.tier_rationale: 768 bytes of colour data with a fixed count; the colours themselves are never inspected and constraining them would make every palettised thumbnail identical.
APP0.palette.description: 256-entry RGB palette for a JFXX extension_code 0x11 thumbnail.
APP0.palette.notes: The count is fixed at 256 by JFIF and by the template, so only the contents are free.

APP0.pixel.tier_rationale: Thumbnail pixel bytes; their values are never examined. The array's length, however, is a real constraint - see the note.
APP0.pixel.description: Palettised thumbnail pixel indices (extension_code 0x11) or raw RGB triples (extension_code 0x13).
APP0.pixel.field_type: uchar[szSection - 8] | struct {uchar r, g, b;}[(ushort)xThumbnail * yThumbnail]
APP0.pixel.notes: TEMPLATE QUIRK: for extension_code 0x11 the template sizes the pixel array from szSection - 8 (line 1135) even though JFIF defines it as xThumbnail * yThumbnail indices, and it has already consumed the two thumbnail dimension bytes and the 768-byte palette. To keep the segment self-consistent a generator must satisfy szSection - 8 = 2 + 768 + xThumbnail*yThumbnail. For extension_code 0x13 (line 1142) the array is correctly sized from the dimensions.

APP0.ByteOrder.tier_rationale: Compared literally by the lookahead at line 1148 and again by Strncmp at line 1156, where it switches the whole parser to little-endian. Anything other than these two strings drops the segment into the 'unknown APP0' branch and no CIFF structure is parsed at all.
APP0.ByteOrder.description: Canon CIFF byte-order mark: 'II' for little-endian, 'MM' for big-endian.

lookahead.note: Line 1148 tests both alternatives and line 1149 additionally requires 'HEAPJPGM' eight bytes later; both conditions must hold for the CIFF branch to open.

APP0.ByteOrder.notes: Canon CIFF in practice is always 'II'. Only 'II' actually switches endianness (line 1156); 'MM' leaves the template in the big-endian mode set at line 1535, so both are consistent.

APP0.HeaderLength.tier_rationale: The directory base is computed as HeaderLength + cifOffset at line 1162 and the directory size as szSection - 2 - HeaderLength at line 1163; a wrong value places the whole CIFF directory at the wrong address and gives it the wrong size, so every entry is read from unrelated bytes.
APP0.HeaderLength.description: Length of the CIFF header, i.e. the offset from the start of the CIFF data to the start of the heap.
APP0.HeaderLength.algorithm: byte offset from cifOffset to the first heap byte
APP0.HeaderLength.covers: the CIFF header itself: ByteOrder[2] + HeaderLength[4] + type[4] + subtype[4] and any header padding
APP0.HeaderLength.notes: CIFF 1.0R4 fixes the header at 26 (0x1A) bytes for a HEAP/JPGM file: the 14 bytes the template names plus a 12-byte version block. Endianness follows ByteOrder, which line 1156 has already applied.

APP0.type.tier_rationale: The lookahead at line 1149 compares the eight bytes at FTell()+6 against 'HEAPJPGM', which is exactly this field followed by subtype. Write anything else and the CIFF branch is never entered.

lookahead.note: ReadStringN(FTell() + 6, 8) spans both type and subtype, so the two fields form one eight-byte literal.

APP0.subtype.tier_rationale: The second half of the eight-byte 'HEAPJPGM' literal tested at line 1149; the same reasoning applies.

APP0.unknown.tier_rationale: The catch-all payload for an APP0 whose signature matches none of the three known layouts; nothing reads it.
APP0.unknown.notes: Reaching this branch requires the first five bytes to differ from both 'JFIF\0' and 'JFXX\0' and the CIFF lookahead at lines 1148-1149 to fail. It is worth reaching: it is the only APP0 branch that leaves the payload entirely free.

APP1.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_APP1 at line 1596; the marker must equal the dispatch value.
APP1.marker.description: APP1 application segment marker, used by EXIF and by XMP.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_APP1 at line 1596.

APP1.szSection.tier_rationale: Line 1229 seeks to offset + szSection - 8 to leave the segment, and the two fallback branches size their payloads as szSection - 31 and szSection - 2. A wrong value leaves the parser inside or past the segment and the next marker is read from the wrong address.
APP1.szSection.description: Length of the APP1 segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
APP1.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the segment payload
APP1.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment
APP1.szSection.notes: For the EXIF branch the payload is 6 signature bytes plus the TIFF block, so szSection = 8 + (size of the TIFF block). The seek at line 1229 uses offset + szSection - 8, where offset is the TIFF header origin - that is, szSection - 8 is exactly the TIFF block length, which confirms the arithmetic. JPEG limits any segment to 65535 bytes, which is why large EXIF payloads are split across multiple APP1 segments in real files.

APP1.EXIF.tier_rationale: The lookahead at line 1178 compares five bytes against 'Exif\0'; the template then consumes six. Write anything else and the entire EXIF sub-parser - IFD chain, sub-IFDs, GPS IFD, maker notes and the embedded thumbnail JPEG - is skipped for the 'unknown APP1' branch.
APP1.EXIF.description: EXIF identifier: the ASCII string 'Exif' followed by two NUL bytes.

lookahead.note: The lookahead compares only five bytes but the field is six; the sixth byte is the pad that EXIF 2.2 requires and that the template consumes without testing.

APP1.EXIF.notes: EXIF 2.2 section 4.7.2 defines the APP1 prefix as 'Exif' 0x00 0x00. Only the first five bytes are tested, so the sixth is technically free - but a real EXIF reader requires it to be zero.

APP1.align.tier_rationale: Line 1182 tests align[0] == 'I' and switches the parser to little-endian; line 1230 switches back. Every multi-byte field in the whole TIFF block - entry counts, tag numbers, offsets - is read in this byte order, so a value that is neither 'II' nor 'MM' leaves the reader guessing and every offset in the IFD chain is read byte-swapped.
APP1.align.description: TIFF byte-order mark opening the EXIF TIFF header: 'II' for little-endian, 'MM' for big-endian.
APP1.align.notes: Both values are equally correct and each drives a different set of byte-swapping paths through any TIFF reader, so both should be emitted. The template only tests align[0], so a malformed 'I?' would also switch to little-endian - real readers require the two bytes to match.

APP1.tagMark.tier_rationale: The TIFF 6.0 magic number. The template's comment at line 1183 names it, and although the template does not test it, every TIFF and EXIF reader does: a block whose third and fourth bytes are not 42 in the declared byte order is rejected as not-a-TIFF and the whole IFD chain is abandoned.
APP1.tagMark.description: TIFF magic number, the 16-bit value 42 written in the byte order given by APP1.align.
APP1.tagMark.notes: Written 0x2A 0x00 when align is 'II' and 0x00 0x2A when align is 'MM'. libjpeg-turbo never looks at APP1, so this gates EXIF consumers (libexif, exiv2, ExifTool, ImageMagick's EXIF reader) rather than the JPEG decoder itself.

APP1.offsetFirstIFD.tier_rationale: Line 1185 tests it against 8 and seeks to offset + offsetFirstIFD when it differs; a wrong value starts the main IFD parse at an arbitrary address, so nDirEntry and every entry after it are read from unrelated bytes.
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.description: Offset from the TIFF header origin to the first IFD; 8 when the IFD immediately follows the eight-byte TIFF header.
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.algorithm: byte offset from the TIFF header origin (the byte holding align[0]) to the first IFD
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.covers: the TIFF header itself: align[2] + tagMark[2] + offsetFirstIFD[4] = 8 bytes
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.notes: 8 is the only value that needs no seek, and line 1185 makes that explicit by testing for it. TIFF 6.0 allows any even offset; larger values leave a gap between the header and the first IFD that a generator would have to fill.

APP1.imageData.tier_rationale: Thumbnail bytes for a non-JPEG-compressed EXIF thumbnail; the template reads thumbLength of them without inspecting any. Their length is derived from a tag value, not constrained here.
APP1.imageData.description: Raw thumbnail data read when the thumbnail IFD declares a Compression other than 6.
APP1.imageData.notes: thumbLength comes from the ThumbnailLength (0x0202) or StripByteCounts (0x0117) tag and the seek target from ThumbnailOffset (0x0201) or StripOffsets (0x0111); see the dependencies section. When Compression is 6 the same bytes are parsed as a complete nested JPEG instead (line 1222).

APP1.XAP.tier_rationale: Compared literally against a 29-byte string by the lookahead at line 1231; anything else takes the 'unknown APP1' branch and the XMP packet is never delimited.
APP1.XAP.description: XMP identifier: the Adobe XMP namespace URI followed by a NUL byte.

lookahead.note: A 29-byte literal comparison - the longest single literal in this template.

APP1.XAP.notes: The string is 28 printable characters plus the terminating NUL, which is why the field is char[29] and the payload after it is szSection - 31 (2 length bytes + 29 signature bytes).

APP1.remain.tier_rationale: The XMP packet body. It should be well-formed XML, but no JPEG decoder parses it and an XMP toolkit that fails to parse it simply drops the metadata rather than rejecting the image, so nothing here gates depth.
APP1.remain.description: XMP packet: an RDF/XML document carried in the APP1 segment after the XMP namespace signature.
APP1.remain.notes: XMP (ISO 16684-1) wraps the RDF in '<?xpacket begin=...?>' ... '<?xpacket end="w"?>'. Emitting a well-formed packet is what lets an XMP-aware consumer walk the RDF tree instead of aborting at the first byte; emitting arbitrary bytes is equally legal as far as the JPEG decoder is concerned. Treated as Tier C because the objective is JPEG-decoder coverage and this payload is invisible to it.

APP1.unknown.tier_rationale: Catch-all payload for an APP1 that is neither EXIF nor XMP; never inspected.

APP2.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_APP2 at line 1599; the marker must equal the dispatch value.
APP2.marker.description: APP2 application segment marker, used by FlashPix and by ICC colour profiles.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_APP2 at line 1599.

APP2.szSection.tier_rationale: All three branches size their payload from it (szSection - 8, szSection - 16, szSection - 2); a wrong value desynchronises the marker stream.
APP2.szSection.description: Length of the APP2 segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
APP2.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the segment payload
APP2.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment
APP2.szSection.notes: For the ICC branch szSection = 16 + len(data): 2 length bytes + 12 signature bytes + block_num + block_total + the profile chunk.

APP2.FPXR.tier_rationale: Compared literally at line 1245; anything else skips the FlashPix branch.

APP2.version.tier_rationale: A FlashPix version byte the template records and never tests.

APP2.remain.tier_rationale: FlashPix payload bytes; never inspected by this template or by a JPEG decoder.
APP2.remain.description: Remaining FlashPix payload after the signature and version byte.

APP2.ICC_PROFILE.tier_rationale: Compared literally against a twelve-byte string at line 1250; anything else and the ICC branch - the only place a colour profile can be attached to a JPEG - is never entered.
APP2.ICC_PROFILE.description: ICC profile identifier: the ASCII string 'ICC_PROFILE' followed by a NUL byte.
APP2.ICC_PROFILE.notes: ICC.1:2010 Annex B.4 defines this embedding. libjpeg-turbo exposes it through jpeg_read_icc_profile(); djpeg does not request it, but ImageMagick, lcms-based readers and browsers do.

APP2.block_num.tier_rationale: ICC profiles longer than about 65500 bytes are split across several APP2 segments; a reader reassembles them by this 1-based index and refuses the profile if the indices are not exactly 1..block_total with no duplicates and no gaps. A wrong index means the profile is discarded and the colour-management path is never entered.
APP2.block_num.description: 1-based index of this APP2 segment within the ICC profile chunk sequence.
APP2.block_num.algorithm: sequence index, counting from 1, of this chunk among the chunks carrying one ICC profile
APP2.block_num.covers: this segment's contribution to the reassembled profile
APP2.block_num.notes: libjpeg's jpeg_read_icc_profile rejects a marker whose seq_no is 0 or greater than num_markers, and rejects the whole profile if any chunk is missing or duplicated. A single-chunk profile has block_num = block_total = 1.

APP2.block_total.tier_rationale: Every chunk of the same profile must declare the same total, and that total must equal the number of chunks actually present; a mismatch makes the reassembly fail and the profile is dropped.
APP2.block_total.description: Total number of APP2 segments carrying this ICC profile.
APP2.block_total.algorithm: count of APP2 ICC_PROFILE segments in the file
APP2.block_total.notes: Must be identical in every chunk of the sequence. The value 1 (a single, self-contained chunk) is both the simplest and the most commonly emitted.

APP2.data.tier_rationale: The bytes of an embedded ICC colour profile. A colour-managed consumer parses the reassembled profile and, if the header is not a valid ICC profile, discards it and falls back to the untagged path - so the whole colour-transform pipeline (profile parsing, tag table walk, curve and matrix evaluation) is skipped before it does any work.
APP2.data.description: One chunk of an ICC colour profile embedded in an APP2 segment; the concatenation of all chunks in block_num order must be a complete ICC profile.
APP2.data.codec: ICC profile (ICC.1:2010 / ICC v2 or v4, as embedded per ICC.1:2010 Annex B.4)
APP2.data.must_produce: The concatenation of every APP2 ICC_PROFILE chunk, in block_num order, must be one ICC profile: a 128-byte header followed by a 4-byte tag count, then that many 12-byte tag table entries (signature, offset, size), then the tag data. In the header, bytes 0-3 are the profile size in big-endian and must equal the total length of the reassembled profile; bytes 12-15 are the device class ('mntr', 'scnr', 'prtr', 'link', 'spac', 'abst', 'nmcl'); bytes 16-19 are the data colour space ('RGB ', 'GRAY', 'CMYK', 'YCbr'); bytes 20-23 are the PCS ('XYZ ' or 'Lab '); bytes 36-39 are the fixed signature 'acsp' (0x61637370); bytes 64-67 are the rendering intent (0-3). All multi-byte header fields are big-endian. Tag offsets are measured from the start of the profile and every tag must lie inside it.
APP2.data.decoder_gate: libjpeg-turbo itself never parses the profile - djpeg decodes the image identically with a valid or a garbage profile. The gate is in the colour-managed consumer: lcms2 (used by ImageMagick, GIMP and browsers) calls cmsOpenProfileFromMem, which checks the 'acsp' signature at offset 36 and the size field at offset 0 and returns NULL on mismatch; the caller then drops the profile and takes the untagged path, so none of the profile parsing, tag-table or transform-building code runs. libjpeg's own jpeg_read_icc_profile additionally refuses the whole sequence if the block_num/block_total chunk indices are inconsistent, before any byte of the profile is examined.
APP2.data.generation_strategy:
Emit a minimal but complete v2 profile of 132 + 12*n + (tag data) bytes. The smallest useful form is a 128-byte header, a tag count of 0, and nothing else - 132 bytes total:
  bytes 0-3    00 00 00 84            profile size = 132
  bytes 4-7    00 00 00 00            preferred CMM (0 is legal)
  bytes 8-11   02 10 00 00            version 2.1.0
  bytes 12-15  'mntr'                 device class
  bytes 16-19  'RGB '                 data colour space
  bytes 20-23  'XYZ '                 PCS
  bytes 24-35  date/time, 6 uint16    any value, e.g. all zero
  bytes 36-39  'acsp'                 THE fixed signature
  bytes 40-43  00 00 00 00            platform (0 is legal)
  bytes 44-99  flags, manufacturer, model, attributes, rendering intent, PCS illuminant
               all may be zero except bytes 68-79, the D50 illuminant, which should be
               00 00 F6 D6 00 01 00 00 00 00 D3 2D
  bytes 100-127 creator and reserved, all zero
  bytes 128-131 00 00 00 00           tag count = 0
Then set block_num = block_total = 1 and szSection = 16 + 132 = 148. A profile carrying real tags is built by appending 12-byte tag table entries and their data and updating both the tag count and the size field at bytes 0-3 - the size field is derived from the payload, never the other way round.
APP2.data.notes: Because a JPEG segment cannot exceed 65535 bytes, a profile larger than about 65519 bytes must be split; each chunk is an independent APP2 segment repeating the 12-byte signature and carrying its own block_num. The chunking is what block_num and block_total describe, and the profile's own internal size field counts the reassembled bytes, not the chunk.

APP2.unknown.tier_rationale: Catch-all payload for an APP2 that is neither FlashPix nor ICC; never inspected.

APP12.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_APP12 at line 1602; the marker must equal the dispatch value.
APP12.marker.description: APP12 application segment marker, used by the Ducky metadata block.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_APP12 at line 1602.

APP12.szSection.tier_rationale: It seeds the loop counter s at line 1268 and bounds the entry chain, and the fallback branch sizes its payload as szSection - 2; a wrong value either truncates the chain or runs it past the end of the segment.
APP12.szSection.description: Length of the APP12 segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
APP12.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the segment payload
APP12.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment
APP12.szSection.notes: TEMPLATE QUIRK: line 1268 initialises the loop budget to the full szSection rather than szSection - 7 (the part after the length and the 'Ducky' signature), so the while loop at line 1269 is willing to walk seven bytes further than the segment actually holds. The loop is really terminated by the DK_End tag test at lines 1277 and 1301, so a generator should always close the chain with an explicit DK_End entry rather than relying on the byte budget.

APP12.Ducky.tier_rationale: Compared literally at line 1265; anything else takes the 'unknown APP12' branch and the tag chain is never parsed.
APP12.Ducky.description: Ducky segment identifier, the five ASCII bytes 'Ducky' (no NUL terminator).

lookahead.note: Unlike the other APPn signatures in this template this one carries no trailing NUL; the comparison is exactly five characters.

APP12.Ducky.notes: Written by Photoshop's 'Save for Web'. ExifTool's APP12.pm documents the same layout.

APP12.entry.tag.tier_rationale: A closed four-value enumeration selecting the entry's payload shape at line 1282, one value of which (DK_End) terminates the chain. All four are legal and each is a distinct branch; DK_End in particular is the loop's only reliable exit, so it can never be dropped.
APP12.entry.tag.description: Ducky entry tag identifying what the entry carries.
APP12.entry.tag.notes: DK_End (0) is special: the template breaks out of the struct at line 1278 before reading a length, so a DK_End entry is two bytes and nothing follows it. Values above 3 reach the default branch at line 1296 and are read as char unknown[len] - legal, and worth emitting, but they do not terminate the chain.

APP12.entry.len.tier_rationale: It sizes the entry's payload in three of the four branches (char comment[len - 4] at lines 1290 and 1294, char unknown[len] at line 1297) and is subtracted from the loop budget through sizeof(entry) at line 1303. A wrong value makes the next entry start in the middle of this one's payload and the whole chain desynchronises.
APP12.entry.len.description: Length in bytes of this Ducky entry's payload, not counting the tag and the length field itself.
APP12.entry.len.algorithm: byte count of the entry payload following the 4-byte tag+len prefix
APP12.entry.len.covers: the bytes after len: 4 for DK_Quality, or 4 + (len - 4) for DK_Comment and DK_Copyright
APP12.entry.len.notes: For DK_Comment and DK_Copyright the template reads a uint32 count and then len - 4 bytes, so len must be at least 4. For DK_Quality the template reads a uint32 value and ignores len entirely, so len should still be 4 to keep the chain consistent. A DK_End entry has no len field at all.

APP12.entry.value.tier_rationale: The Ducky quality number; nothing tests it and a reader only displays it.
APP12.entry.value.description: JPEG quality value carried by a DK_Quality entry.
APP12.entry.value.notes: In files written by Photoshop this is 1..100, but no reader enforces it and the field is a full uint32.

APP12.entry.count.tier_rationale: A four-byte prefix on the Ducky comment and copyright entries that the template reads and never uses; it does not size the comment array, which is sized from len - 4 instead.
APP12.entry.count.description: Leading uint32 of a DK_Comment or DK_Copyright entry.

APP12.entry.comment.tier_rationale: Free text; its length is derived from len and its contents are never examined.
APP12.entry.comment.description: Comment or copyright text carried by a DK_Comment or DK_Copyright entry.

APP12.entry.unknown.tier_rationale: Payload of an unrecognised Ducky tag; never inspected.
APP12.entry.unknown.description: Uninterpreted payload of a Ducky entry whose tag is not one of the four defined values.

APP12.unknown.tier_rationale: Catch-all payload for an APP12 that is not a Ducky block; never inspected.

APP13.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_APP13 at line 1605; the marker must equal the dispatch value.
APP13.marker.description: APP13 application segment marker, used by Photoshop Image Resource Blocks and by IPTC.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_APP13 at line 1605.

APP13.szSection.tier_rationale: It seeds remainsize at line 1318, which bounds the IRB chain at line 1319 and sizes the escape payload at line 1325; the two fallback branches size their payloads from it directly. A wrong value truncates or overruns the block chain.
APP13.szSection.description: Length of the APP13 segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
APP13.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the segment payload
APP13.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment
APP13.szSection.notes: remainsize starts at szSection - 16 (line 1318), i.e. the 2 length bytes plus the 14-byte signature, less two more - so the template's own budget is two bytes short of the payload. The chain is bounded by remainsize -= sizeof(block) at line 1353, so a generator must make the blocks sum to exactly szSection - 16 for the loop to end cleanly.

APP13.photoshop30.tier_rationale: Compared literally against a 14-byte string at line 1315; anything else takes one of the two fallback branches and no Image Resource Block is parsed.
APP13.photoshop30.description: Photoshop IRB identifier: the ASCII string 'Photoshop 3.0' followed by a NUL byte.

APP13.block.type.tier_rationale: Tested at lines 1322 and 1323. A value that is none of the four makes the template consume the rest of the segment as opaque bytes and break out of the chain at line 1326, so every block after it is lost - the four-character signature is what keeps the chain walkable.
APP13.block.type.description: Image Resource Block signature; '8BIM' is Photoshop's own, the other three are the legacy signatures the template accepts.
APP13.block.type.notes: TEMPLATE QUIRK: line 1322 compares a char[4] against the five-byte literal "8BIM" (four characters plus the C string terminator). In 010 Editor this comparison succeeds on the four characters, but it is worth knowing the literal is one byte longer than the field. The 8BIM branch and the PHUT/DCSR/AgHg branch have identical (empty) bodies, so all four behave the same here; they differ only in that a fifth value escapes the loop.

APP13.block.unknown.tier_rationale: The escape payload consumed when the block signature is unrecognised; never inspected.
APP13.block.unknown.description: Remainder of the APP13 payload, swallowed when a block signature is none of the four accepted values.

APP13.block.tag.tier_rationale: A closed enumeration of Photoshop resource identifiers. The template does not switch on it, but an IPTC- or Photoshop-aware consumer does, and several of these resources are themselves structured blobs (IPTC records, an ICC profile, a JPEG thumbnail, an XMP packet). Every value is a distinct branch in such a reader and none is refused.
APP13.block.tag.description: Photoshop Image Resource identifier saying what this block carries.
APP13.block.tag.notes: Hex values: 0x0404, 0x0406, 0x0409, 0x040a, 0x040b, 0x040c, 0x040f, 0x0419, 0x0422, 0x0424, 0x0425, 0x0bb7. Photoshop defines many more resource ids (the full range 0x0400-0x0bb7 plus path resources 0x07d0-0x0bb6); this is the set the template names and a value outside it is still parsed correctly, because the template reads namelen/size generically. PS_PhotoshopThumbnail (0x040c) carries a complete JPEG datastream and PS_ICC_Profile (0x040f) carries an ICC profile, so those two blocks' data fields have the same internal contracts as APP2.data and the top-level scan.

APP13.block.namelen.tier_rationale: A Pascal-string length: it sizes name[] at line 1344 and its parity decides whether a pad byte follows at line 1345. A wrong value shifts everything after it, so size and data are read from the wrong offsets and the block chain desynchronises.
APP13.block.namelen.description: Length in bytes of the block's Pascal-style name string.
APP13.block.namelen.algorithm: byte count of the name string that follows, not counting this length byte
APP13.block.namelen.notes: Photoshop pads the name so that the length byte plus the name occupies an even number of bytes, which is what line 1345 implements: a pad byte is emitted when namelen is even (namelen % 2 != 1). Most real blocks use namelen 0, which makes the name absent and the pad present. Note that lines 1344 and 1346 both declare fields conditionally, so a generator must reproduce the parity rule exactly.

APP13.block.name.tier_rationale: A free-text resource name; nothing inspects it.
APP13.block.name.description: Optional Pascal-style name for the Image Resource Block.

APP13.block.padding.tier_rationale: An alignment pad byte whose value the Photoshop specification leaves undefined and which no reader inspects; whether it is present is determined by parity, but what it contains is free.
APP13.block.padding.description: Pad byte keeping the name field and the data field on even boundaries.
APP13.block.padding.notes: Two distinct declarations share this name: line 1346 pads the name to an even length and line 1351 pads the data. Both are emitted conditionally on a parity test, so their presence is fully determined while their contents are free. Photoshop writes 0x00.

APP13.block.size.tier_rationale: It sizes data[] at line 1349 and its parity decides the trailing pad at line 1350; the whole block's footprint enters the chain budget through sizeof(block) at line 1353. A wrong value makes the next block start inside this one's data.
APP13.block.size.description: Length in bytes of this Image Resource Block's data payload.
APP13.block.size.algorithm: byte count of the resource data that follows
APP13.block.size.covers: the data[] array at line 1349, not the trailing pad byte
APP13.block.size.notes: A pad byte follows when size is odd (line 1350: size % 2 != 0), so the block always occupies an even number of bytes. The data field is omitted entirely when size is 0 (line 1348), in which case no pad is emitted either - a generator must reproduce both conditions.

APP13.block.data.tier_rationale: The resource payload. For most resource ids it is opaque bytes that no JPEG decoder reads. Two ids do carry structured payloads, but a consumer that fails to parse them drops the resource rather than refusing the image, so nothing here gates depth.
APP13.block.data.description: Image Resource Block payload; its meaning is given by block.tag.
APP13.block.data.notes: Two ids carry payloads with real internal contracts: PS_PhotoshopThumbnail (0x040c) begins with a 28-byte thumbnail header (format, width, height, widthbytes, total size, compressed size, bits per pixel, number of planes - all big-endian uint32/uint16) followed by a complete JPEG datastream, and PS_ICC_Profile (0x040f) carries a bare ICC profile with the same contract as APP2.data. PS_IPTCData (0x0404) carries IPTC IIM records, each 0x1C 'marker' + record + dataset + length. None of these is required for the image to decode.

APP13.adobe_cm.tier_rationale: Compared literally at line 1355; anything else takes the final fallback branch.
APP13.adobe_cm.description: Adobe colour-management APP13 identifier: the ASCII string 'Adobe_CM' followed by a NUL byte.

APP13.AdobeCMType.tier_rationale: A single byte the template reads and never tests; no consumer refuses a file over it.
APP13.AdobeCMType.notes: Line 1358 then tests szSection != 12 and emits the remainder as char unknown[szSection - 12], so an Adobe_CM segment of exactly 12 bytes has no trailing data.

APP13.unknown.tier_rationale: Catch-all payload for an APP13 that is neither a Photoshop IRB nor an Adobe_CM block; never inspected.
APP13.unknown.notes: Two declarations share the name: line 1359 inside the Adobe_CM branch (sized szSection - 12) and line 1362 in the final else (sized szSection - 2).

APP14.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_APP14 at line 1608; the marker must equal the dispatch value.
APP14.marker.description: APP14 application segment marker, used by the Adobe DCT colour-transform block.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_APP14 at line 1608.

APP14.szSection.tier_rationale: Line 1377 computes the trailing payload as szSection + startof(szSection) - FTell(), so the segment's end address is derived entirely from this value; and libjpeg-turbo only examines an APP14 as an Adobe block when the segment is at least 14 bytes long, so a short length means the colour transform is silently ignored.
APP14.szSection.description: Length of the APP14 segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
APP14.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the segment payload
APP14.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment
APP14.szSection.notes: The canonical Adobe APP14 is 14 bytes: 2 length + 5 signature + 2 version + 2 flag0 + 2 flag1 + 1 transform. libjpeg's examine_app14 requires datalen >= 12 (the payload after the length) before it reads the transform byte, so szSection must be at least 14 for the Adobe_transform to take effect.

APP14.adobe.tier_rationale: Compared literally at line 1370, and libjpeg-turbo independently checks the same five bytes in examine_app14 before it will set saw_Adobe_marker. Without them the colour-transform byte is never read and the decoder falls back to guessing the colour space from the component count.
APP14.adobe.description: Adobe DCT segment identifier, the five ASCII bytes 'Adobe' (no NUL terminator).

lookahead.note: Five characters with no terminator, like the Ducky signature and unlike the other APPn signatures.

APP14.version.tier_rationale: The Adobe DCTEncodeVersion word; libjpeg reads past it without testing it and the template never looks at it.

APP14.flag0.tier_rationale: An Adobe flags word that no decoder tests; pinning it would remove the only free bits in an otherwise fully determined segment.

APP14.flag1.tier_rationale: As for flag0: recorded, never tested.

APP14.color_transform_code.tier_rationale: This single byte re-routes libjpeg's colour-space selection: for a 3-component frame it chooses between JCS_RGB (0) and JCS_YCbCr (1), and for 4 components between JCS_CMYK (0) and JCS_YCCK (2). Each choice selects a different colour-conversion routine and, for YCCK, an extra inverse-YCC pass. Measured as not fatal for any value, so Tier B - but it is one of the highest-value diversity fields in the whole format.
APP14.color_transform_code.description: Adobe colour transform applied by the encoder: 0 = none (RGB or CMYK), 1 = YCbCr, 2 = YCCK.

measured_gate.observed: 3-component frame with transform 0, 1, 2, 3 and 255: all rc=0, image decoded. 4-component frame with transform 1: rc warns 'Unknown Adobe color transform code 1' and still decodes.
measured_gate.conclusion: Never fatal. Values above 2 reach libjpeg's JWRN_ADOBE_XFORM warning path, which is itself worth reaching, but 0/1/2 are the three that select a real colour-conversion routine.

APP14.color_transform_code.notes: Without an Adobe APP14 libjpeg infers the colour space from the component count alone: 1 -> grayscale, 3 -> YCbCr, 4 -> CMYK. So emitting the segment at all is what opens the alternative interpretations - a 3-component frame with transform 0 is decoded as raw RGB, which no other combination produces.

APP14.unknown.tier_rationale: Trailing bytes of an over-long Adobe segment, or the whole payload of a non-Adobe APP14; never inspected.
APP14.unknown.notes: Two declarations share the name: line 1377 inside the Adobe branch, whose length is computed from the segment end, and line 1380 in the else branch.

SOS.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_SOS at line 1550. This is also the marker that ends header parsing and starts the entropy-coded data, so it is the hinge of the whole file: libjpeg reports 'Invalid JPEG file structure: missing SOS marker' if it reaches EOI without one.
SOS.marker.description: Start Of Scan marker, introducing the scan header and the entropy-coded data that follows it.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_SOS at line 1550, after which the template locates the EOI with FindFirst at line 1553 and terminates the marker loop by setting bEOI.

measured_gate.observed: A file whose EOI appears before any SOS: rc=1 'Invalid JPEG file structure: missing SOS marker'
measured_gate.conclusion: At least one SOS is mandatory.

SOS.szSection.tier_rationale: libjpeg checks this length exactly: get_sos requires length == nr_comp * 2 + 6 and raises JERR_BAD_LENGTH otherwise. Measured: a single byte either way is fatal.
SOS.szSection.description: Length of the SOS header in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
SOS.szSection.covers: szSection[2] + nr_comp[1] + comp[nr_comp]*2 + Ss[1] + Se[1] + Ah/Al[1]

measured_gate.observed: szSection -2, -1, +1 and +10 all rc=1 'Bogus marker length'
measured_gate.conclusion: Exact agreement with nr_comp is required; there is no tolerance in either direction.

SOS.nr_comp.tier_rationale: Measured: 5 or more components in one scan is fatal - 'Bogus marker length', because libjpeg's get_sos tests n > MAX_COMPS_IN_SCAN (4) in the same condition as the length check. 0 fails the same test. The legal set is exactly 1..4, so this is a Tier A gate whose legal set happens to have four members - all four must be emitted, because 1 gives a non-interleaved scan and 2..4 give interleaved scans with different MCU geometry.
SOS.nr_comp.description: Number of image components in this scan (Ns in ITU-T T.81).

measured_gate.observed: Ns=1,2,3,4 all decode; Ns=5 rc=1 'Bogus marker length' (MAX_COMPS_IN_SCAN = 4)
measured_gate.conclusion: 1..4 exactly. Ns=1 selects the non-interleaved data-unit path in the entropy decoder; Ns>1 selects the interleaved MCU path. These are different loops in decode_mcu and both matter.

SOS.nr_comp.notes: Also listed in diversity_axes: the value is pinned to a four-member set by the decoder, but which of the four a file uses is a free choice that changes the MCU geometry and therefore the whole shape of the entropy-coded segment. Ns must be <= the frame's nr_comp, and every component listed must match a component declared in the frame header.

COMPSOS.compId.tier_rationale: Measured free across the whole byte range: 0, 1 and 200 all decode, and duplicate ids across components decode too. What matters is not the value but that it matches one of the ids in the frame header - an agreement recorded as a dependency, not as a narrowing of this field.
COMPSOS.compId.description: Scan component selector: identifies which frame component this scan entry refers to, by matching a COMPS.compId in the frame header.

measured_gate.observed: SOF ids [1] with SOS id [1]: rc=0. SOF ids [1] with SOS id [2]: rc=1 'Invalid component ID 2 in SOS'. SOF ids [0] with SOS id [0]: rc=0. SOF ids [200] with SOS id [200]: rc=0. SOF ids [1,1,1] with SOS ids [1,1,1]: rc=0.
measured_gate.conclusion: The value itself is unconstrained; the agreement with the frame header is the gate. Pin the agreement, not the value.

COMPSOS.AC.tier_rationale: A Huffman table destination selector. libjpeg's jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl refuses any index outside 0..3 with JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE, and refuses an index whose table was never defined with the same error - in both cases before a single MCU is decoded.
COMPSOS.AC.description: Entropy coding table destination selector, high nibble of the scan component's table byte.
COMPSOS.AC.notes: TEMPLATE BUG: the names are swapped. ITU-T T.81 defines the byte as Td in the high nibble (DC table selector) and Ta in the low nibble (AC table selector). Because BitfieldLeftToRight is in force (line 57), the first-declared bitfield takes the most significant bits, so the field the template calls 'AC' is physically the high nibble and therefore carries Td, the DC selector - and the field it calls 'DC' carries Ta. The template's own history line 13 records a COMPSOS fix in 1.6.4, but the naming was left reversed. The constraint is identical for both fields, so generation is unaffected; only the interpretation is. Baseline JPEG (SOF0) additionally restricts both selectors to 0 and 1; extended and progressive frames allow all four.

COMPSOS.DC.tier_rationale: The companion table selector, subject to the same JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE check in libjpeg: out of range 0..3, or in range but never defined by a DHT, and decoding stops before any MCU.
COMPSOS.DC.description: Entropy coding table destination selector, low nibble of the scan component's table byte.
COMPSOS.DC.notes: See the note on COMPSOS.AC: by T.81 this low nibble is Ta, the AC table selector, despite the field name. In a progressive DC-only scan the AC selector is unused and may be any value; in a progressive AC scan the DC selector is unused.

SOS.Ss.tier_rationale: Its legal set depends entirely on the frame type, and getting it wrong is fatal for two of the four frame types but only a warning for the other two - so it fails the Tier A test in general while having a genuinely finite legal set. Measured: with a sequential frame a wrong value produces 'Invalid SOS parameters for sequential JPEG' and libjpeg silently overrides it; with SOF2 or SOF3 a wrong value is fatal.
