SOS.Ss.description: Start of spectral selection in a progressive scan, or the predictor selector in a lossless frame; must be 0 for a sequential frame.

measured_gate.observed: Sequential (SOF0): Ss=0 rc=0; Ss=1, 5, 63 and 64 all rc=2 'Invalid SOS parameters for sequential JPEG', image still decoded. Progressive (SOF2), single scan: Ss=0 Se=0 rc=0; Ss=0 Se=63 rc=1 'Invalid progressive/lossless parameters Ss=0 Se=63 Ah=0 Al=0'; Ss=1 Se=63 rc=2 'Inconsistent progression sequence for component 0 coefficient 0'. Lossless (SOF3): Ss=1..7 rc=0; Ss=0 and Ss=8 rc=1 'Invalid progressive/lossless parameters'.
measured_gate.conclusion: Sequential: must be 0 or you get a warning and an override. Progressive: 0..63 with Se constrained against it. Lossless: 1..7, where Ss is the predictor selector and anything else is fatal.

SOS.Ss.notes: The dependencies section carries the per-frame-type rule. The full 0..63 span is recorded here because a progressive frame genuinely uses all of it.

SOS.Se.tier_rationale: Same shape as Ss: finite legal set, fatal for progressive and lossless frames, warning-and-override for sequential ones.
SOS.Se.description: End of spectral selection in a progressive scan; must be 63 for a sequential frame and 0 for a lossless frame.
SOS.Se.notes: T.81 requires Se >= Ss and Se <= 63; in a progressive DC scan Ss and Se must both be 0, and in a progressive AC scan Ss must be >= 1 and the scan must name exactly one component. In a lossless frame Se is unused and conventionally 0.

SOS.Ah.tier_rationale: The successive-approximation high bit position: a four-bit field whose legal span is 0..13, meaningful only in progressive frames where it distinguishes a first scan (Ah=0) from a refinement scan (Ah>0). Each selects a completely different entropy decoder in libjpeg, so the whole span belongs in the set.
SOS.Ah.description: Successive approximation bit position high, high nibble of the final SOS byte.
SOS.Ah.notes: T.81 limits Ah and Al to 0..13. Ah must be 0 in a sequential frame (libjpeg warns and overrides otherwise) and in the first progressive scan for a given coefficient band; in a refinement scan Ah must equal the Al of the preceding scan for that band, which is what libjpeg's 'Inconsistent progression sequence' check enforces. Measured: Ah/Al = 0x11 in a sequential frame gives rc=2 'Invalid SOS parameters for sequential JPEG' and the image still decodes.

SOS.Al.tier_rationale: The successive-approximation low bit position, with the same 0..13 span; in a lossless frame it is the point transform instead. Both roles are real and neither is refused in a sequential frame.
SOS.Al.description: Successive approximation bit position low, low nibble of the final SOS byte; the point transform in a lossless frame.

measured_gate.observed: SOF2 single DC scan with Al=1: rc=0, image decoded. SOF3 lossless with Al=0: rc=0.
measured_gate.conclusion: Al is free within 0..13; a progressive DC scan with Al>0 is a legal 'successive approximation' first scan.

UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.tier_rationale: Every marker the dispatch switch does not name reaches this struct through the default case at line 1617. The set is finite (the M_ID enumeration minus the routed markers) and the choice matters enormously: measured, some of these markers open whole alternative decoders in libjpeg-turbo and others are fatal. Recording only the safe ones would delete the arithmetic-coding decoder from the reachable set; recording none would delete the branch entirely.
UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.description: Marker of a segment the template does not model structurally; the segment is consumed as a length plus opaque bytes.

measured_gate.observed: Inserted before the SOS and measured one at a time: 0xFFDC DNL rc=0; 0xFFFE COM rc=0; APP1 0xFFE1, APP12 0xFFEC, APP13 0xFFED, APP14 0xFFEE all rc=0; 0xFF01 TEM rc=0; 0xFFD0 RST0 rc=0; 0xFFCC DAC rc depends on the conditioning values ('Bogus DAC value 0x4' when the DC low nibble exceeds the high nibble, rc=0 otherwise). FATAL: 0xFFDE DHP 'Unsupported marker type 0xde'; 0xFFDF EXP 'Unsupported marker type 0xdf'; 0xFFF7 JPGLS 'Unsupported marker type 0xf7'; 0xFFC8 JPG 'Unsupported JPEG process: SOF type 0xc8'; 0xFFC5/C6/C7 and 0xFFCD/CE/CF 'Unsupported JPEG process'; a second 0xFFD8 SOI 'Invalid JPEG file structure: two SOI markers'; an 0xFFD9 EOI before the SOS 'Invalid JPEG file structure: missing SOS marker'.
measured_gate.conclusion: The marker choice splits three ways: tolerated and skipped (APPn, COM, DNL, TEM, RSTn), parsed by a real sub-decoder (DAC at 0xFFCC, and the arithmetic frame headers 0xFFC9/0xFFCA), or fatal (0xFFC5-C7, 0xFFCD-CF, 0xFFC8, 0xFFDE, 0xFFDF, 0xFFF7). The preferred set names the non-fatal ones; the fatal ones stay in valid_values because a file that exercises the decoder's rejection path is still a file, and because this is the template's only route to them.

UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.notes: The value must additionally satisfy the guard at line 1618, ReadUByte(FTell()) == 0xff, or the template consumes a single garbage byte instead. Markers 0xFFD0-0xFFD9 and 0xFF01 are standalone in ITU-T T.81 - they carry no length field - so routing them through this struct, which unconditionally reads a WORD szSection, produces a segment that does not match the standard. That is a template limitation, recorded here rather than hidden: a generator that emits them through this path emits two extra bytes that a decoder will read as the start of the next marker.

UNKNOWN.szSection.tier_rationale: It is the only thing that says how many bytes to skip; line 1406 guards against it running past the end of the file and line 1410 sizes the payload as szSection - 2. A wrong value resynchronises the whole marker stream at the wrong offset.
UNKNOWN.szSection.description: Length of the unmodelled segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
UNKNOWN.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + size of the opaque payload
UNKNOWN.szSection.covers: from the first byte of szSection to the last byte of the segment
UNKNOWN.szSection.template_parse_requirement: Line 1406 tests FTell() + szSection - 2 >= JpegFileEnd and, when true, emits ubyte unknown[JpegFileEnd - FTell()] with a Warning instead of the declared length. A generator should keep the segment inside the file so the normal branch at line 1410 is taken; the guard exists because the template must tolerate truncated input, not because the format permits it.

UNKNOWN.unknown.tier_rationale: The template declares this as opaque bytes, but for several marker values libjpeg-turbo parses it as a real segment body with its own validation. Measured: with UnknownMarker = 0xFFC9 or 0xFFCA these bytes are a frame header that routes the file into the arithmetic entropy decoder - an entire alternative decoder that no other path in this template can reach - and with 0xFFCC they are arithmetic conditioning tables that are range-checked and can abort the file. Random bytes under those markers stop the decode before any image data is processed.
UNKNOWN.unknown.description: Body of a segment the template does not model; its required contents depend on UnknownMarker.
UNKNOWN.unknown.codec: marker-specific segment body (ITU-T T.81 clause B.2), selected by UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker
UNKNOWN.unknown.must_produce:
Per marker value:
  0xFFC9 / 0xFFCA / 0xFFCB (arithmetic SOF): the identical layout to a Huffman frame header - P[1], Y[2], X[2], Nf[1], then Nf triples of Ci[1], Hi/Vi[1], Tqi[1]. Length must be 8 + 3*Nf.
  0xFFCC (DAC, arithmetic conditioning): zero or more 2-byte pairs of Tc/Tb[1], Cs[1]. Tc is the high nibble (0 = DC, 1 = AC) and Tb the low nibble (table 0..3). For a DC table (Tc=0) the low nibble of Cs must be <= its high nibble; for an AC table Cs must be 1..63. Length must be 2 + 2*(number of pairs).
  0xFFDC (DNL): exactly one 2-byte big-endian number of lines. Length must be 4.
  0xFFDE (DHP) and 0xFFDF (EXP): hierarchical-progression bodies, which libjpeg-turbo refuses outright.
  0xFFE3-0xFFEF, 0xFFF0-0xFFFD (unhandled APPn and JPGn): free-form; no decoder inspects them.
UNKNOWN.unknown.decoder_gate: Measured with libjpeg-turbo 3.x djpeg. With UnknownMarker = 0xFFC9 and a well-formed frame-header body, a file carrying no DHT at all and 40 bytes of 0x55 as its scan decoded to a full image (rc=0 at 64x64, rc=2 'Corrupt JPEG data: 29 extraneous bytes before marker 0xd9' at 16x16) - the arithmetic decoder ran. With a malformed body the frame header fails length validation and the file is refused with 'Bogus marker length' before any decoding. With UnknownMarker = 0xFFCC and a conditioning pair whose DC low nibble exceeds its high nibble, the file is refused with 'Bogus DAC value 0x4'.
UNKNOWN.unknown.generation_strategy:
Choose the body from the marker.
  For 0xFFC9 (arithmetic sequential, the highest-value case) emit exactly what a SOFx body would be:
    08                       precision = 8
    HH HH                    Y = number of lines, big-endian, derived from the same free dimension
    WW WW                    X = samples per line, big-endian
    01                       Nf = 1
    01 11 00                 component 1, H=1 V=1, quantization table 0
  and set szSection = 11. Follow it with an ordinary DQT defining table 0 and an ordinary SOS; no DHT is needed, because arithmetic coding uses the conditioning tables instead, and the default conditioning is used when no DAC segment is present. The entropy-coded bytes that follow may be arbitrary - the arithmetic decoder does not reject them - so this is the cheapest way to reach jdarith.c.
  For 0xFFCC emit pairs such as 00 40 (DC table 0, Cs = 0x40, low nibble 0 <= high nibble 4) and 10 05 (AC table 0, Cs = 5), giving szSection = 6.
  For 0xFFDC emit the two-byte line count and szSection = 4.
  For every other marker in the set, free bytes of any length are correct.
UNKNOWN.unknown.notes: This entry exists because checklist item 3 asks what must be inside every opaque byte array, and for this one the honest answer is 'it depends on the marker, and for three marker values it matters a great deal'. The arithmetic-frame case is the single most valuable thing in this entry: the template's dispatch switch routes only M_SOF0 through M_SOF3 to the SOFx struct, so 0xFFC9-0xFFCB can only be produced through this path, and they are the only route to libjpeg-turbo's arithmetic decoder.

DHT.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_DHT at line 1572; the marker must equal the dispatch value.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_DHT at line 1572.

DHT.szSection.tier_rationale: It is the loop budget: huffsz = szSection - 2 at line 1417 and huffsz -= sizeof(huff_table) at line 1430, so the number of tables in the segment is decided entirely by this value. Measured: -1 gives 'Bogus Huffman table definition' (the last table is cut short) and +1 gives 'Bogus marker length'; both are fatal.
DHT.szSection.description: Length of the DHT segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
DHT.szSection.algorithm: 2 + sum over the tables in this segment of (1 + 16 + sum(length[0..15]))
DHT.szSection.covers: szSection[2] plus, for each table, htInfo[1] + length[16] + HTV[sum of length]

measured_gate.observed: szSection -2 and -1 => rc=1 'Bogus Huffman table definition'; +1 and +10 => rc=1 'Bogus marker length'
measured_gate.conclusion: Exact agreement with the tables present is required. A single segment may legally carry several tables - measured up to 8 - and each adds 17 + sum(length) bytes.

DHT.szSection.notes: One DHT segment may define any number of tables back to back; measured 1, 2, 4 and 8 tables in a single segment, all rc=0. Redefining the same htInfo twice simply overwrites the earlier table.

Huffmann_Table.htInfo.tier_rationale: Measured as a hard gate with an exact eight-value legal set: libjpeg's get_dht strips bit 4 to decide class and then tests the remaining index against NUM_HUFF_TBLS (4), raising 'Bogus DHT index N' for anything else. 0x04 gives 'Bogus DHT index 4', 0x20 gives 'Bogus DHT index 32', 0xFF gives 'Bogus DHT index 239' - all fatal before any image data is touched.
Huffmann_Table.htInfo.description: Huffman table class and destination: high nibble Tc (0 = DC/lossless, 1 = AC), low nibble Th (destination 0-3).

measured_gate.observed: 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13 => rc=0. 0x04 => 'Bogus DHT index 4'; 0x14 => 'Bogus DHT index 4'; 0x20 => 'Bogus DHT index 32'; 0x30 => 'Bogus DHT index 32'; 0xFF => 'Bogus DHT index 239'. All fatal.
measured_gate.conclusion: Exactly the eight values. Note that the reported index for 0x14 is 4, confirming that libjpeg subtracts 0x10 before range-checking, so the class bit is bit 4 and bits 5-7 must be zero.

Huffmann_Table.htInfo.notes: Baseline JPEG (SOF0) allows only destinations 0 and 1, so a baseline file uses at most 0x00, 0x01, 0x10, 0x11; extended, progressive and arithmetic frames allow all four destinations. The class matters for the symbol constraint - see Huffmann_Table.HTV.

Huffmann_Table.length.tier_rationale: These sixteen bytes are not data, they are a canonical Huffman code specification, and libjpeg validates them before decoding anything. Measured: a violating table produces 'Bogus Huffman table definition' with rc=1 and no output at all. Random bytes here fail almost surely - a uniformly random set of sixteen counts overflows the code space with probability very close to 1 - so this is the single highest-value constraint in the format, and it is one the .bt gives no hint of.
Huffmann_Table.length.description: Counts of Huffman codes of each length from 1 to 16 bits, defining the shape of a canonical Huffman code.
Huffmann_Table.length.codec: canonical Huffman code specification (ITU-T T.81 Annex C, figures C.1-C.3; validated by libjpeg's jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl)
Huffmann_Table.length.must_produce:
Let n_l = length[l-1] be the number of codes of length l, for l = 1..16. Two conditions must hold:
  (1) SYMBOL COUNT: sum over l of n_l must be <= 256, and should be >= 1.
  (2) CODE SPACE (the 'no all-ones codeword' rule): define c_0 = 0 and c_l = (c_{l-1} << 1) + n_l. For every length l between the smallest and the largest length that has a non-zero count, c_l must be STRICTLY LESS THAN 2^l. Equivalently, the Kraft sum sum(n_l / 2^l) taken over lengths 1..l must be strictly less than 1 at every such l - a code that exactly fills the code space is rejected, because T.81 reserves the all-ones codeword.
Note that condition (2) means a table cannot have two codes of length 1: c_1 = 2 is not < 2. An all-zero length[] is accepted as an empty table but then every code in the scan is invalid.
Huffmann_Table.length.decoder_gate: libjpeg-turbo 3.x, measured. jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl raises JERR_BAD_HUFF_TABLE, 'Bogus Huffman table definition', and djpeg exits with rc=1 having written no output whatsoever. Observed directly: length=[2,0,...] (two 1-bit codes) rejected; [3,0,...] rejected; [0,5,0,...] rejected; [16]*16 (sum 256, code space overflowed) rejected; [0,1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,0,...] (sum exactly 256, a full code) rejected at length 5; sum 300 rejected on the symbol count. Accepted: [1,0,...], [0,2,0,...], [0,0,...,0,2]. The predicate above was checked against djpeg by exhaustive enumeration of all 624 tables with counts 0-4 at lengths 1-4: zero disagreements.
Huffmann_Table.length.generation_strategy:
The simplest correct table - the JPEG analogue of a deflate stored block - is a single one-bit code:
  length = 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
  HTV    = 00
This assigns symbol 0x00 the codeword '0' and satisfies both conditions (c_1 = 1 < 2). Verified: a complete 176-byte JPEG built on it decodes silently to a uniform image.
The next simplest, which gives two usable symbols, is:
  length = 00 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
  HTV    = 00 01
assigning symbol 0x00 the codeword '00' and symbol 0x01 the codeword '01' (c_2 = 2 < 4).
To build a table of arbitrary shape safely, pick counts greedily: start with c = 0, and for each length l from 1 to 16 choose n_l anywhere in 0 .. (2^l - 1 - c), then set c = 2*(c + n_l). Stopping early leaves a short table; the residual code space is simply unused, which is legal. This derives the table from whatever shape is wanted rather than forcing a fixed table.
The standard Annex K example tables are also valid and are what real encoders emit; they are worth emitting sometimes because they exercise libjpeg's fast multi-bit lookup path, whereas a one-symbol table always hits the short-code path.
Huffmann_Table.length.notes: sum(length) is also the size of the HTV array that follows (line 1428 computes sumLen in the loop at lines 1425-1427), so these sixteen bytes decide the segment's length. This is the clearest case in the format of the rule that a payload is derived from a declared value: HTV and szSection are both computed from length[], never the reverse.

Huffmann_Table.HTV.tier_rationale: The symbol list of the Huffman table. Its length is fixed by length[] and, for a DC table, its contents are validated: measured, a DC table containing any symbol above 15 is refused with 'Bogus Huffman table definition' and rc=1, no output. AC tables accept the full byte range.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.description: Huffman symbol values, listed in order of increasing code length and, within a length, in the order the codes are assigned.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.codec: Huffman symbol list (ITU-T T.81 Annex C; DC symbols are magnitude categories per Table F.1, AC symbols are run/size bytes per Table F.2)
Huffmann_Table.HTV.must_produce:
Exactly sum(length[0..15]) bytes. The i-th byte is the symbol that receives the i-th canonical codeword.
  DC tables (htInfo high nibble 0): every symbol must be 0..15. The symbol is the magnitude category SSSS, and it says how many additional raw bits follow the codeword in the scan (0 bits for category 0, which means a difference of exactly zero).
  AC tables (htInfo high nibble 1): every byte 0x00..0xFF is legal. The high nibble is the zero run length RRRR and the low nibble is the magnitude category SSSS. 0x00 is EOB (end of block) and 0xF0 is ZRL (a run of sixteen zeros). A symbol whose low nibble is 0 and whose high nibble is neither 0 nor 15 is meaningless in a sequential scan but is a valid EOBn run marker in a progressive scan.
Symbols should be distinct - duplicates make one codeword unreachable but are not rejected.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.decoder_gate: libjpeg-turbo 3.x, measured. A DC table whose symbol list contains 16 or 255 is refused with 'Bogus Huffman table definition', rc=1, no output - libjpeg-turbo validates DC symbols against the 0..15 magnitude-category range. The identical table declared as an AC table (htInfo 0x10) with symbol 255 decodes normally, rc=0. A symbol list shorter or longer than sum(length) is not detectable as such: it simply shifts the segment and produces 'Bogus marker length' or a corrupt following table.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.generation_strategy: For the minimal DC table emit the single byte 00 (magnitude category 0, meaning 'difference is zero', which needs no extra bits). For the minimal AC table emit the single byte 00 (EOB, meaning 'the rest of this block is zero'). Those two symbols are all that the all-zeros scan construction needs.\nFor a fuller DC table emit the categories in increasing order, 00 01 02 03 ... up to 0F at most.\nFor a fuller AC table emit 00 (EOB) first, then run/size bytes such as 01 02 03 11 12 21 31 41 F0, and make sure the count matches sum(length) exactly. Whatever symbols are chosen, the scan must then encode only symbols that appear in the table - the scan is derived from the table, not the table from the scan.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.notes: The template computes the array size correctly by summing length[] (lines 1423-1428), so a generator that emits sumLen bytes is automatically consistent with the template's own parse.

DQT.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_DQT at line 1575; the marker must equal the dispatch value.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_DQT at line 1575.

DQT.szSection.tier_rationale: It is the loop budget: qtsz = szSection - 2 at line 1437 and qtsz -= sizeof(qtable) at line 1448. Measured: -1 gives 'Bogus marker length' and +1 makes the parser read the next segment's first byte as another table's Pq/Tq, producing 'Bogus DQT index 15'. Both fatal.
DQT.szSection.description: Length of the DQT segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
DQT.szSection.algorithm: 2 + sum over the tables in this segment of (1 + 64 * (Pq == 0 ? 1 : 2))
DQT.szSection.covers: szSection[2] plus, for each table, the Pq/Tq byte and its 64 coefficients

measured_gate.observed: szSection -2 and -1 => rc=1 'Bogus marker length'; +1 and +10 => rc=1 'Bogus DQT index 15'
measured_gate.conclusion: Exact agreement required. Measured 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 tables in a single segment, all rc=0, so the per-table loop is real and a generator may pack several tables into one segment.

DQT.szSection.notes: A single-table 8-bit segment is 67 bytes (2 + 1 + 64); a 16-bit one is 131.

QuanTable.Pq.tier_rationale: The element precision. Measured: both 0 (8-bit entries) and 1 (16-bit entries) decode cleanly, and they select different read loops in the decoder and different array types in the template (line 1444 versus line 1446). Neither is refused, so Tier B, and both belong in the set.
QuanTable.Pq.description: Quantization table element precision: 0 = one byte per coefficient, 1 = two bytes per coefficient.

measured_gate.observed: Pq=0 with 8-bit values, and Pq=1 with 16-bit values up to 65535 and down to 0: all rc=0
measured_gate.conclusion: Both precisions work. libjpeg treats any non-zero high nibble as 16-bit, so values 2-15 behave like 1, but T.81 defines only 0 and 1.

QuanTable.Pq.notes: T.81 forbids Pq = 1 in a baseline (SOF0) frame; 16-bit tables are for extended and progressive frames only. libjpeg-turbo does not enforce that restriction. With BitfieldLeftToRight in force Pq is the high nibble, which matches T.81.

QuanTable.Tq.tier_rationale: Measured as a hard gate: libjpeg's get_dqt tests the destination against NUM_QUANT_TBLS (4) and raises 'Bogus DQT index N' for anything larger - Tq=4 and Tq=15 both fatal, rc=1, no output. The legal set is exactly 0..3 and all four are usable.
QuanTable.Tq.description: Quantization table destination identifier, referenced by COMPS.compNr in the frame header.

measured_gate.observed: Tq=0,1,2,3 => rc=0. Tq=4 => 'Bogus DQT index 4'. Tq=15 => 'Bogus DQT index 15'. Both fatal.
measured_gate.conclusion: Exactly 0..3. Baseline JPEG additionally restricts a frame to at most two distinct tables, but libjpeg does not enforce that.

QuanTable.qTable.tier_rationale: The 64 quantization coefficients. This is the field most likely to be pinned to a 'standard' table, and measurement says it must not be: every value from 0 to 255 (and to 65535 at Pq=1) decodes cleanly, including all-zero, which does not even produce a divide-by-zero. The coefficients scale every dequantized value, so varying them varies the whole IDCT input range and reaches different saturation and range-limiting paths in the output stage.
QuanTable.qTable.description: The 64 quantization step sizes, stored in zig-zag order.

measured_gate.observed: All coefficients 0: rc=0. All 1: rc=0. All 255: rc=0. Pq=1 with all 65535: rc=0. Pq=1 with all 0: rc=0.
measured_gate.conclusion: Entirely free. T.81 says the values shall not be zero, but libjpeg-turbo multiplies rather than divides during dequantization, so zero is harmless and is worth emitting.

QuanTable.qTable.notes: Two declarations share the name: line 1444 (byte[64], Pq=0) and line 1446 (uint16[64], Pq=1). The 16-bit form is big-endian. The zig-zag ordering means element i of the array is coefficient jpeg_natural_order[i] of the block, but since the contents are free the ordering only matters to a consumer inspecting the table, not to the generator.

DRI.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_DRI at line 1578; the marker must equal the dispatch value.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_DRI at line 1578.

DRI.szSection.tier_rationale: libjpeg's get_dri tests length != 4 and raises JERR_BAD_LENGTH; the segment has exactly one 16-bit payload field so the length is completely determined.
DRI.szSection.description: Length of the DRI segment; always 4.
DRI.szSection.notes: This is the one szSection in the whole template whose value is fixed rather than computed.

DRI.Ri.tier_rationale: The restart interval in MCUs. Measured free across the whole 16-bit span: 0, 1, 2, 4 and 100 all decode cleanly when the scan carries matching RST markers. This is a textbook case of the central rule - it is a count that the entropy-coded payload must agree with, so the payload is derived from it. Narrowing it would fix how often the decoder's restart resynchronisation path runs, which is one of the few control-flow branches in the entropy decoder that a generator can steer directly.
DRI.Ri.description: Number of MCUs between restart markers; 0 disables restart markers entirely.

measured_gate.observed: Ri = 0, 1, 2, 4 and 100 with matching RSTn markers in the scan: all rc=0, full image. Ri = 2 with NO RSTn markers in the scan: rc=2 'Corrupt JPEG data: 21 extraneous bytes before marker 0xd9', image still produced.
measured_gate.conclusion: Every value is legal. A mismatch between Ri and the markers actually present costs only a warning, but it truncates the scan at the first missing restart, so a file that derives its RST markers from Ri decodes far more of its own data.

DRI.Ri.notes: Ri = 1 puts a restart marker after every single MCU, which is the most aggressive exercise of the restart path and is completely legal. See JPGFILE.scanData for how the markers are derived from this value.

DHP.marker.tier_rationale: Reached only from case M_DHP at line 1581; the marker must equal the dispatch value.
DHP.marker.description: Define Hierarchical Progression marker, which carries a frame-header-shaped body describing the largest frame of a hierarchical sequence.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_DHP at line 1581.

measured_gate.observed: Any file containing an 0xFFDE segment: rc=1 'Unsupported marker type 0xde', no output at all.
measured_gate.conclusion: The entire DHP branch is a dead end for libjpeg-turbo coverage: hierarchical JPEG is not implemented and the marker is rejected outright, before the image is decoded. The branch is still recorded in full because the template models it and because a decoder that does implement hierarchical mode (or one being tested for its rejection path) needs the structure. A generator aiming at libjpeg-turbo line coverage should emit this marker rarely.

DHP.szSection.tier_rationale: The body has the same shape as a frame header, so the length is fully determined by Nf; a decoder that implements DHP applies the same length check as for SOF.
DHP.szSection.description: Length of the DHP segment in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
DHP.szSection.covers: szSection[2] + P[1] + Y[2] + X[2] + Nf[1] + component_param[Nf]*3

DHP.P.tier_rationale: Sample precision for the hierarchical sequence. T.81 allows 8 and 12 for DCT-based hierarchical modes and 2..16 for lossless ones; the set is finite and no value can be shown to be refused by libjpeg because the marker never gets that far.
DHP.P.description: Sample precision in bits for the hierarchical frame sequence.

evidence.note: ITU-T T.81 clause B.3.2: the DHP segment has the same parameters as a frame header, so P takes the same values as the frame header's precision - 8 or 12 for DCT-based processes and 2 to 16 for lossless processes.

DHP.Y.tier_rationale: A declared image height; it sizes nothing in this template and the marker is rejected before it is used, so constraining it buys nothing and removes variety from the segment body.
DHP.Y.description: Number of lines in the largest frame of the hierarchical sequence.

DHP.X.description: Number of samples per line in the largest frame of the hierarchical sequence.

DHP.Nf.tier_rationale: The component count and the bound of the component_param array. It is a repeat count, so it stays free and the segment length is derived from it.
DHP.Nf.description: Number of image components in the hierarchical frame.
DHP.Nf.notes: T.81 allows 1..255. szSection must be 8 + 3*Nf; the output_budget on the DHP structure rule bounds the total, not this field.

DHP.component_param.id.tier_rationale: A component identifier whose value is arbitrary; only its agreement with later frame headers matters, and that is a cross-segment rule, not a narrowing of this field.
DHP.component_param.id.description: Component identifier within the hierarchical frame.

DHP.component_param.h_factor.tier_rationale: A sampling factor with the same 1..4 legal span T.81 gives every frame header; all four values are legal and each changes the MCU geometry a hierarchical decoder would build.
DHP.component_param.h_factor.description: Horizontal sampling factor, high nibble of the component's sampling byte.

DHP.component_param.v_factor.description: Vertical sampling factor, low nibble of the component's sampling byte.

DHP.component_param.Tq.tier_rationale: T.81 clause B.3.2 states that Tq shall be zero in a DHP segment, because DHP describes frame geometry only and specifies no quantization. A decoder implementing hierarchical mode checks it in the same way it checks the frame-header Tq against NUM_QUANT_TBLS.
DHP.component_param.Tq.description: Quantization table destination selector; required to be 0 in a DHP segment.

evidence.note: ITU-T T.81 clause B.3.2: 'Tqi: ... in the DHP segment this parameter shall be zero.'

SOFx.marker.tier_rationale: This one struct serves four dispatch cases (lines 1584, 1587, 1590, 1593), so the marker must be one of exactly four values and must match the case that selected it. It is also the single most consequential byte in the file: it chooses the decoding process, and measured, each of the four leads somewhere different, while the values outside the set that reach this struct's shape are fatal.
SOFx.marker.description: Start Of Frame marker; its low nibble identifies the coding process for the frame that follows.

lookahead.note: Four separate cases at lines 1584, 1587, 1590 and 1593 all instantiate SOFx, into the distinct instance names sof0, sof1, sof2 and sof3.

measured_gate.observed: 0xFFC0 baseline: rc=0. 0xFFC1 extended sequential: rc=0. 0xFFC2 progressive: rc=0 only when the scan carries valid progressive parameters (a single DC scan with Ss=0 Se=0 works; Ss=0 Se=63 gives a fatal 'Invalid progressive/lossless parameters'). 0xFFC3 lossless: rc=0 only when Ss is the predictor 1..7; a full 8-bit, 12-bit and even 16-bit lossless frame all decoded. Outside the set: 0xFFC5, 0xFFC6, 0xFFC7, 0xFFCD, 0xFFCE, 0xFFCF all rc=1 'Unsupported JPEG process: SOF type 0x..'; 0xFFC9 and 0xFFCA (arithmetic) decode but can only be reached through the UNKNOWN path, since the switch does not route them here.
measured_gate.conclusion: All four routed values reach a real decoder, but SOF2 and SOF3 additionally constrain the scan header - see the dependencies. SOF1 is the cheapest way to leave baseline behind, and SOF3 opens libjpeg-turbo's lossless decoder, an entirely separate code path from the DCT one.

SOFx.marker.notes: The template routes only these four of the twelve SOF markers. M_SOF5 through M_SOF7, M_SOF9 through M_SOF11 and M_SOF13 through M_SOF15 fall to the default case at line 1617 and are emitted through the UNKNOWN struct instead; of those, only the arithmetic trio 0xFFC9-0xFFCB is decodable, and UNKNOWN.unknown documents how to reach it.

SOFx.szSection.tier_rationale: libjpeg's get_sof tests length != nr_comp * 3 + 8 and raises JERR_BAD_LENGTH. Measured: every perturbation of -2, -1, +1 and +10 is fatal with 'Bogus marker length'.
SOFx.szSection.description: Length of the frame header in bytes, counting the two length bytes but not the marker.
SOFx.szSection.covers: szSection[2] + precision[1] + Y_image[2] + X_image[2] + nr_comp[1] + comp[nr_comp]*3

measured_gate.observed: szSection -2, -1, +1 and +10 all rc=1 'Bogus marker length'
measured_gate.conclusion: Exact agreement with nr_comp is required in both directions.

SOFx.precision.tier_rationale: Measured as a hard gate whose legal set depends on the frame type. For SOF0, SOF1 and SOF2, libjpeg-turbo accepts exactly 8 and 12 and refuses everything else with 'Unsupported JPEG data precision N', rc=1, no output. 12 is not a curiosity: libjpeg-turbo 3.x compiles a complete second instantiation of the DCT, quantization and colour pipeline for 12-bit samples, so emitting it doubles the reachable decoder. For SOF3 the legal set widens to 2..16, all of which were measured to decode.
SOFx.precision.description: Sample precision in bits for the components of this frame.

measured_gate.observed: SOF0/SOF1/SOF2 at precision 2, 4, 9, 16 and 255: rc=1 'Unsupported JPEG data precision N'. At 8 and 12: rc=0, and the 12-bit output was visibly wider (140-byte PGM versus 75-byte). SOF3 at precision 2, 4, 8, 12 and 16: all decoded, output sizes 73, 74, 75, 140 and 141 bytes.
measured_gate.conclusion: Two disjoint legal sets, selected by the frame marker. The dependencies section carries the rule. Emitting 12 wherever it is legal is one of the cheapest large coverage gains in this format.

SOFx.precision.notes: T.81 allows 8 and 12 for the DCT-based processes and 2..16 for lossless. The union is recorded here and the per-marker split is a dependency, so that a generator emitting SOF3 is not restricted to the DCT set.

SOFx.Y_image.tier_rationale: The image height, and the field that most directly decides how much entropy-coded data the file needs. This is precisely the field whose GIF counterpart was narrowed to powers of two and cost 1.7 points. The scan payload must be computed from it; it must never be shrunk so that a precomputed scan fits. Measured free across 1..65500 with the payload derived.
SOFx.Y_image.description: Number of lines in the image (Y in ITU-T T.81).

measured_gate.observed: Heights 1, 3, 13, 23, 64, 255, 300, 480 and 65500 all decoded cleanly with a derived scan. Height 0: rc=1 'Empty JPEG image (DNL not supported)'. Height 65535: rc=1 'Maximum supported image dimension is 65500 pixels'.
measured_gate.conclusion: Free across essentially the whole 16-bit span. Two values fail: 0, which T.81 permits only when a DNL marker supplies the height later and which libjpeg-turbo does not implement, and anything above libjpeg's JPEG_MAX_DIMENSION of 65500. NO MINIMUM OR MAXIMUM IS RECORDED FOR THIS FIELD and none may be added: a file with height 0 is a legitimate file that exercises the decoder's rejection path, and the 65500 ceiling is one decoder's build-time limit, not a property of the format. The number of MCU rows, and therefore the size of the entropy-coded segment, is computed from whatever value is chosen.

SOFx.Y_image.notes: MCU rows = ceil(Y_image / (8 * Vmax)) where Vmax is the largest COMPS.Vert in the frame. See JPGFILE.scanData.

SOFx.X_image.tier_rationale: The image width; the same reasoning as Y_image applies in full. Derive the scan from it, never the reverse.
SOFx.X_image.description: Number of samples per line in the image (X in ITU-T T.81).

measured_gate.observed: Widths 1, 3, 7, 17, 37, 255, 300, 640, 1000 and 65500 all decoded cleanly with a derived scan; width 0 rejected as 'Empty JPEG image'; width 65535 rejected as above.
measured_gate.conclusion: Free. Narrow and wide images take different paths through libjpeg's upsampling and colour-conversion inner loops, and an image narrower than one MCU exercises the edge-padding path, so the extremes are valuable rather than wasteful.

SOFx.X_image.notes: MCU columns = ceil(X_image / (8 * Hmax)) where Hmax is the largest COMPS.Horz in the frame.

SOFx.nr_comp.tier_rationale: Measured as a hard gate at the top: 11 or more components gives 'Too many color components: N, max 10', rc=1, no output, because libjpeg's MAX_COMPONENTS is 10. Zero fails the JERR_EMPTY_IMAGE check. So the legal set is exactly 1..10 - but which of the ten a file uses is a completely free choice that reshapes the entire decoder pipeline, so all ten belong in the set and the field is also a diversity axis.
SOFx.nr_comp.description: Number of image components in the frame (Nf in ITU-T T.81); sizes the comp[] array.

measured_gate.observed: Nf = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 10 all decoded - the failures at 2, 4, 5, 6 and 10 were djpeg's output writer refusing to write a non-grayscale, non-RGB file ('PPM output must be grayscale or RGB'), which happens after jpeg_start_decompress has already succeeded. Nf = 11, 20 and 255: rc=1 'Too many color components: N, max 10'.
measured_gate.conclusion: 1..10 exactly. The colour-space inference makes 1, 3 and 4 special - they become GRAYSCALE, YCbCr and CMYK respectively and each selects a different colour-conversion routine - while 2 and 5..10 become JCS_UNKNOWN and take the null-conversion path, which is itself a distinct branch worth reaching.

SOFx.nr_comp.notes: A scan may name at most 4 of these components (SOS.nr_comp), so a frame with more than 4 components needs more than one scan - which this template cannot express, because the marker loop terminates at the first SOS (line 1567). A generator emitting nr_comp > 4 therefore produces a frame whose remaining components are never scanned; libjpeg still decodes what it was given. Also listed in diversity_axes.

COMPS.compId.tier_rationale: Measured free across the whole byte range, duplicates included. Its only obligation is that the scan header names the same values, which is a cross-field agreement recorded as a dependency rather than a narrowing here.
COMPS.compId.description: Component identifier, used by the scan header to select this component.

measured_gate.observed: Frame ids [0], [1], [200] and [1,1,1] all rc=0; only a scan naming an id absent from the frame fails, with 'Invalid component ID 2 in SOS'.
measured_gate.conclusion: The value is free; the agreement is the gate. JFIF conventionally uses 1, 2, 3 and Adobe uses 'R','G','B' (0x52, 0x47, 0x42), and both work.

COMPS.Horz.tier_rationale: Measured as a hard gate: 0 and 5 both give 'Bogus sampling factors', rc=1, no output, because libjpeg checks against MAX_SAMP_FACTOR = 4. The legal set is exactly 1..4 and every value in it changes the MCU geometry and selects a different upsampling routine, so all four must be emitted.
COMPS.Horz.description: Horizontal sampling factor, high nibble of the component's sampling byte (Hi in ITU-T T.81).

measured_gate.observed: H=1,2,3,4 with the other components at 1x1: H=1,2 and 4 decoded; H=3 with V=3 gave 'Sampling factors too large for interleaved scan'; H=4 with V=4 gave the same; H=4 with V=2 decoded. H=0 and H=5 gave 'Bogus sampling factors'.
measured_gate.conclusion: 1..4 individually, with a second, joint constraint: the total number of blocks in one MCU, sum over the scan's components of Hi*Vi, must not exceed libjpeg's MAX_BLOCKS_IN_MCU of 10. That joint rule is recorded as a dependency because it cannot be expressed as a per-field value set.

COMPS.Horz.notes: Common real values are 1 and 2 (2x2, 2x1 and 1x1 subsampling); 3 and 4 are legal and rare, which makes them exactly the values a narrowing pass would discard.

COMPS.Vert.tier_rationale: The same measured gate as COMPS.Horz: 0 and 5 are fatal with 'Bogus sampling factors'; 1..4 are legal.
COMPS.Vert.description: Vertical sampling factor, low nibble of the component's sampling byte (Vi in ITU-T T.81).
COMPS.Vert.notes: Subject to the same joint MAX_BLOCKS_IN_MCU <= 10 rule as COMPS.Horz.

COMPS.compNr.tier_rationale: Despite its name this is Tq, the quantization table destination selector, and it is a hard gate twice over: the value must be 0..3, and the table it names must already have been defined by a DQT. Measured: a frame component naming table 1 when only table 0 was defined gives 'Quantization table 0x01 was not defined', rc=1, no output at all.
COMPS.compNr.description: Quantization table destination selector for this component (Tqi in ITU-T T.81), selecting one of the tables defined by a DQT segment.

measured_gate.observed: Frame Tq=0..3 with a matching DQT: rc=0. Frame Tq=1 with only table 0 defined: rc=1 'Quantization table 0x01 was not defined'. Frame Tq=4: rc=1 'Quantization table 0x04 was not defined'. Omitting the DQT entirely: rc=1 'Quantization table 0x00 was not defined'.
measured_gate.conclusion: Both the range and the reference are gates. The DQT dependency is the strongest required-section rule in the format - stronger than DHT, which libjpeg-turbo can default.

COMPS.compNr.notes: TEMPLATE MISNAMING: the field is the third byte of the frame component specification, which T.81 calls Tqi and which selects a quantization table. The name 'compNr' suggests a component index, which it is not - the component index is its position in the comp[] array and the component identifier is compId. Compare the DHP struct at line 1469, where the template names the same byte Tq correctly.

Nothing inspects it - the template only copies it to a local buffer to print it, replacing embedded NULs with 'x' (line 1499), and libjpeg skips the segment entirely. So a generator emitting Nf > 1 must place the remaining 3*(Nf-1) bytes in the uknown array itself. szSection = 11 with Nf = 1 is the only fully modelled case.

JPGLS.precision.description: Bits per sample for the JPEG-LS frame.
JPGLS.precision.notes: The template's own comment on line 1510 reads 'bits per sample'.

JPGLS.Y_numlines.tier_rationale: The JPEG-LS image height; a dimension, free for exactly the reasons given on SOFx.Y_image.
JPGLS.Y_numlines.description: Number of lines in the JPEG-LS image.

JPGLS.X_numcols.tier_rationale: The JPEG-LS image width; free for the same reasons.
JPGLS.X_numcols.description: Number of columns in the JPEG-LS image.

JPGLS.Nf.tier_rationale: A component count; it is a repeat count and stays free, with the segment length derived from it.

JPGLS.C_compID.tier_rationale: A component identifier whose value is arbitrary, exactly as in a DCT frame header.
JPGLS.C_compID.description: Component identifier for the first (and only modelled) JPEG-LS component.

JPGLS.sub_sampling.tier_rationale: The byte packs the horizontal and vertical sampling factors into two nibbles, each with the legal span 1..4 that T.87 inherits from T.81; the legal byte values are therefore the sixteen combinations, not the full 256.
JPGLS.sub_sampling.description: Packed sampling factors for the JPEG-LS component: high nibble horizontal, low nibble vertical.
JPGLS.sub_sampling.notes: The sixteen values are 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14, 0x21 ... 0x44 - every combination of a horizontal nibble 1..4 with a vertical nibble 1..4. 0x11 (no subsampling) is overwhelmingly the common case in JPEG-LS.

JPGLS.Tq.tier_rationale: The template's own comment on line 1516 states 'always 0', and T.87 confirms it: JPEG-LS defines no quantization tables, so the Tq byte of every component specification shall be zero. A JPEG-LS decoder that finds a non-zero value rejects the frame.
JPGLS.Tq.description: Quantization table selector; always zero in a JPEG-LS frame.

JPGLS.uknown.tier_rationale: Trailing bytes of a JPEG-LS header longer than the single component specification the template models; nothing here inspects them.
JPGLS.uknown.description: Remaining bytes of the JPEG-LS frame header beyond the first component specification.
JPGLS.uknown.notes: For a well-formed multi-component JPEG-LS header these bytes are the remaining component specifications, three bytes each; see the template limitation on JPGLS.szSection. The field name is spelled 'uknown' in the template.

JPGFILE.SOIMarker.tier_rationale: The file's magic number. Measured: libjpeg refuses anything else outright - 'Not a JPEG file: starts with 0x00 0x01' - before reading a single further byte. Four bytes of leading garbage are enough to kill the file even though this template tolerates them.
JPGFILE.SOIMarker.description: Start Of Image marker; must be the first two bytes of the file.

lookahead.note: Selects case M_SOI at line 1546. Note that this is a case in the general marker loop, not a special first-iteration check, so the template is willing to accept an SOI anywhere - or none at all.

measured_gate.observed: A well-formed file: rc=0. The same file with four bytes 00 01 02 03 prepended: rc=1 'Not a JPEG file: starts with 0x00 0x01'. With the SOI removed so the file begins at APP0: rc=1 'Not a JPEG file: starts with 0xff 0xe0'. With FFD8 replaced by FFD7: rc=1 'Not a JPEG file: starts with 0xff 0xd7'. A second SOI inserted later: rc=1 'Invalid JPEG file structure: two SOI markers'.
measured_gate.conclusion: The strictest rule in the format: FFD8 must be the first two bytes and must appear exactly once. The template's tolerance of leading garbage (the 'char garbage' branch at line 1621) and of a repeated SOI is a parser convenience with no counterpart in the decoder.

JPGFILE.scanData.tier_rationale: This is the image. The template declares it as an opaque char array sized by a search for the EOI marker, and says nothing whatever about its contents - exactly the situation checklist item 3 is about. Two things are true at once: the byte-stuffing framing is a hard gate that random data fails about half the time, and the Huffman correctness decides whether the decoder runs its real coefficient pipeline or its error-concealment path. Both matter, and neither is visible anywhere in the .bt.
JPGFILE.scanData.description: Entropy-coded image data: the Huffman-coded, byte-stuffed MCU stream that carries the picture.
JPGFILE.scanData.codec: JPEG entropy-coded segment (ITU-T T.81 Annex F: Huffman-coded MCUs with 0xFF byte stuffing per clause B.1.1.5)
JPGFILE.scanData.must_produce:
The bytes between the SOS header and the next marker are the entropy-coded segment. Two separate requirements apply, and they have very different consequences.

(1) FRAMING - a hard gate. Inside the entropy-coded data every 0xFF byte must be followed by a 0x00 stuffing byte. An 0xFF followed by anything else is read as a marker: if it is a legal one the scan ends there, and if it is not, the decode aborts. This is the one part of the payload that random bytes cannot satisfy.

(2) CODE VALIDITY - depth, not a gate. The bit stream is a sequence of Huffman codewords drawn from the tables the scan header selects. For each data unit, in MCU order: one DC codeword from the component's DC table, followed by SSSS additional raw bits giving the DC difference, then AC codewords from the component's AC table until either 63 coefficients have been accounted for or an EOB symbol (0x00) is emitted. Bits are packed most-significant-first. The number of data units is fixed by the frame geometry and must be produced in full.

MCU COUNT, the value the payload is derived from:
  Let Hmax and Vmax be the largest COMPS.Horz and COMPS.Vert among the components of the frame.
  Interleaved scan (SOS.nr_comp > 1):
    mcus_x = ceil(X_image / (8 * Hmax)), mcus_y = ceil(Y_image / (8 * Vmax))
    each MCU holds, for each scan component in order, Hi * Vi data units
  Non-interleaved scan (SOS.nr_comp == 1):
    compW = ceil(X_image * Hi / Hmax), compH = ceil(Y_image * Vi / Vmax)
    the MCU is one data unit and there are ceil(compW / 8) * ceil(compH / 8) of them

(3) RESTART MARKERS. If a DRI segment set Ri to a non-zero value, then after every Ri MCUs - but not after the final one - the bit stream is padded to a byte boundary with 1-bits and a two-byte marker 0xFF 0xD0+(n mod 8) is written, n counting from 0. Restart markers are NOT byte-stuffed. The DC predictors reset to zero at each restart.

(4) TERMINATION. The final partial byte is padded with 1-bits, and the EOI marker follows.
JPGFILE.scanData.decoder_gate:
libjpeg-turbo 3.x, measured directly.
  Random bytes in place of the entropy-coded segment: the image is still produced in full - a 32x32 3-component file yielded the complete 3085-byte PPM every time - with 'Corrupt JPEG data: bad Huffman code' warnings, because libjpeg's error concealment fills the remaining blocks with grey and carries on. But in 2 of 5 random trials the garbage happened to contain an 0xFF followed by a non-zero byte and the run ended fatally with 'Unsupported marker type 0x2b' and 'Unsupported marker type 0x1d', rc=1.
  An explicitly unstuffed 0xFF 0x7F in the scan: rc=1, 'Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment' then the fatal 'Unsupported marker type 0x7f'.
  So the framing rule is a genuine gate that random data fails roughly half the time, while the Huffman correctness is not a gate at all - it decides WHICH code runs. Valid codewords drive decode_mcu, HUFF_DECODE's fast and slow paths, jpeg_huff_decode, the sign-extension helper, the AC coefficient and EOB-run loops, and then real dequantization and a full IDCT on non-zero input. Garbage drives the error-recovery path, the warning emitter and an IDCT on an all-zero block. Both are coverage and both should appear, but only the valid form reaches the arithmetic core of the decoder.
  Missing DHT: NOT fatal in libjpeg-turbo - rc=2, full image - because it substitutes the standard Annex K tables. Missing DQT IS fatal: 'Quantization table 0x00 was not defined', rc=1, no output.
JPGFILE.scanData.generation_strategy:
The simplest correct construction, and the exact analogue of a deflate stored block or an LZW clear-code run, is an all-zeros scan: every DC difference zero and every block terminated immediately by EOB. It is valid, it is a handful of bits per block, and it decodes to a uniform mid-grey image.

Pair it with the minimal Huffman tables from Huffmann_Table.length:
  DC table: length = 01 00 00 ... 00, HTV = 00   -> symbol 0x00 has the 1-bit codeword '0'
  AC table: length = 01 00 00 ... 00, HTV = 00   -> symbol 0x00 has the 1-bit codeword '0'
Then each data unit costs exactly two bits, both zero: the DC codeword for magnitude category 0 (which requires no additional bits, because category 0 means a difference of exactly zero) and the AC codeword for EOB.

Algorithm:
  1. n = the MCU count from the formula above; emit the data units of each MCU in scan-component order.
  2. For each data unit append the DC codeword bits, then the AC EOB codeword bits, MSB first.
  3. Whenever a whole byte has accumulated, append it; if that byte is 0xFF, append 0x00 after it.
  4. If Ri != 0, at each Ri-MCU boundary pad the current byte with 1-bits, flush it, and append 0xFF 0xD0+(n mod 8) unstuffed.
  5. At the end pad the last partial byte with 1-bits and flush.

Worked example, 16x16, three components all 1x1, the two minimal tables above, Ri = 0:
  Hmax = Vmax = 1, so mcus_x = mcus_y = 2 and there are 4 MCUs, each holding 3 data units - 12 data units, 2 bits each, 24 bits, 3 bytes: 00 00 00. The complete file is 176 bytes and djpeg decodes it silently to a 16x16 image of RGB (128,128,128).

VERIFIED end to end against libjpeg-turbo djpeg at 1x1, 7x13, 37x23, 17x19, 64x64, 300x1, 1x300, 255x255 and 640x480; with 1, 3 and 4 components; with sampling factors 1x1, 2x1, 2x2 and 4x2; and with restart intervals 0, 4 and 10. Every case returned rc=0 with no warnings and a full-size output image.

To add variety without losing validity, keep the framing and vary the contents: use richer Huffman tables and emit non-zero DC categories (a category of s is followed by s raw bits) and AC run/size symbols. Every such choice is free - see content_is_free - as long as every codeword emitted exists in the selected table and the data-unit count still matches the geometry.
JPGFILE.scanData.notes: THE CENTRAL RULE FOR THIS FORMAT: the payload is computed from the dimensions, the component count, the sampling factors and the restart interval. Not one of those fields may be narrowed so that a precomputed scan fits - that is the mistake that cost 1.7 points on GIF, and JPEG offers exactly the same temptation, because the MCU count is a product of four free fields. Every one of them is listed in diversity_axes.\nTEMPLATE NOTE: the array's length comes from FindFirst(M_EOI, ...) at line 1553, a forward search for the first FFD9. A scan whose data happens to contain FFD9 therefore ends early as far as this template is concerned. The byte-stuffing rule mostly prevents that - a stuffed FF is always followed by 00 - but a restart marker sequence never produces FFD9, so a correctly built scan is safe. The template's history entry for version 1.6.2 (line 15) records that the search was changed from backwards to forwards for exactly this reason.

JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.tier_rationale: The same entropy-coded segment, in the branch taken when no EOI marker exists anywhere after the SOS (FindFirst returns -1 at line 1554). The contents are governed by the same codec and the same byte-stuffing gate; only the termination differs.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.description: Entropy-coded image data running to the end of the file because no EOI marker follows it.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.codec: JPEG entropy-coded segment (ITU-T T.81 Annex F), unterminated
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.must_produce: Identical to JPGFILE.scanData in every respect except that no EOI marker follows: the same MCU count derived from the same fields, the same 0xFF byte stuffing, the same restart marker placement, the same 1-bit padding of the final byte. The file simply ends.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.decoder_gate: libjpeg-turbo 3.x, measured. A complete, correct file with its trailing FFD9 removed: rc=2, 'Premature end of JPEG file', and the full image was still produced. So a missing EOI is a warning, not a gate - which makes this branch cheap to reach and worth reaching, because it runs libjpeg's input-suspension and fake-EOI path (jdmarker's fill_input_buffer inserting a synthetic EOI) that a well-terminated file never touches.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.generation_strategy: Build the scan exactly as for JPGFILE.scanData, then stop - emit no EOI. The template reaches this branch whenever no FFD9 appears after the SOS, so a generator selects it simply by omitting the trailing marker. Because this is also the branch that sets bEOI and ends the marker loop (line 1567), nothing may follow it.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.notes: Line 1557 prints 'Missing End of File marker'. This branch and the scanData branch are mutually exclusive.

JPGFILE.EOIMarker.tier_rationale: The value is pinned absolutely: the template does not merely declare it, it locates it by searching for it (FindFirst(M_EOI, ...) at line 1553) and sizes scanData from the result, so writing anything else makes the preceding array the wrong length. Whether the marker is present at all is a separate question, and measurement says its absence is only a warning.
JPGFILE.EOIMarker.description: End Of Image marker, terminating the entropy-coded data.

measured_gate.observed: File with EOI: rc=0. File with the EOI removed: rc=2 'Premature end of JPEG file', full image still produced. File with a second EOI appended: rc=0. File with 44 bytes of trailing garbage after the EOI: rc=0, decoded normally.
measured_gate.conclusion: Present-and-correct is the right default, but the marker is not a gate and everything after it is ignored. That makes the trailing region a free place to put bytes - see JPGFILE.unknownPadding.

JPGFILE.EOIMarker.notes: Unlike every other marker in this template the EOI has no case in the dispatch switch; it is consumed only here, inside the SOS branch. An EOI encountered at top level falls through to the default case at line 1617 and is parsed as an UNKNOWN segment, which reads two bytes after it as a length - a template artefact, since T.81 gives the EOI no length field.

JPGFILE.unknownPadding.tier_rationale: Bytes after the EOI. Measured: libjpeg ignores them completely and decodes the image normally, so nothing here can fail and every byte value is equally legal. It is the only region of a JPEG file with no structure at all.
JPGFILE.unknownPadding.description: Trailing bytes between the EOI marker and the end of the file.

measured_gate.observed: 44 bytes of ASCII appended after the EOI: rc=0, image decoded identically. A second FFD9 appended: rc=0.
measured_gate.conclusion: Entirely ignored. Emitted only when JpegFileEnd - FTell() is non-zero (line 1565).

JPGFILE.unknownPadding.notes: Real cameras and editors leave thumbnails, padding and even second JPEG streams here, so a consumer that scans past the EOI has real code to exercise.

JPGFILE.garbage.tier_rationale: A single byte consumed when the parser is not positioned at a marker - the template's resynchronisation mechanism, added in version 1.6.1 (line 18) so that inter-segment garbage does not fail the parse. Its value is by definition arbitrary; the only thing that matters is that it is not 0xFF, which is what the guard at line 1618 tests.
JPGFILE.garbage.description: One byte of inter-segment filler, consumed when the next byte is not 0xFF and so cannot begin a marker.

measured_gate.observed: Four garbage bytes before the SOI: rc=1 'Not a JPEG file'. Garbage between segments after a valid SOI: libjpeg resynchronises with 'Corrupt JPEG data: N extraneous bytes before marker 0x..' and continues, rc=2.
measured_gate.conclusion: Tolerated between segments, fatal before the SOI. A generator may emit these bytes freely inside the marker stream to exercise libjpeg's next_marker resynchronisation loop, which a clean file never enters - but must never emit one before the SOI.

JPGFILE.garbage.notes: Must not be 0xFF: the guard at line 1618 routes 0xFF to the UNKNOWN struct instead. Any of the other 255 byte values reaches this branch.

dependencies.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: precision 2, 4, 9, 16 and 255 all give 'Unsupported JPEG data precision N' and rc=1 under SOF0, SOF1 and SOF2; 8 and 12 both decode. 12-bit selects libjpeg-turbo 3.x's separate 12-bit instantiation of the whole sample pipeline.
