then.detail: SOS.nr_comp must not exceed SOFx.nr_comp, and must not exceed 4

dependencies.description: A scan may name at most four components and never more than the frame declares.
dependencies.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: SOS.nr_comp = 5 gives rc=1 'Bogus marker length', because get_sos tests n > MAX_COMPS_IN_SCAN in the same condition as the length check. A frame with more than four components therefore needs multiple scans, which this template cannot express.

then.detail: the sum over the scan's components of Horz*Vert must not exceed 10

dependencies.description: An interleaved scan's MCU may contain at most ten data units in total.
dependencies.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: three components at 4x4, 1x1, 1x1 (16+1+1 = 18 blocks) gives rc=1 'Sampling factors too large for interleaved scan'; 3x3, 1x1, 1x1 (9+1+1 = 11) gives the same; 4x2, 1x1, 1x1 (8+1+1 = 10) decodes. libjpeg's MAX_BLOCKS_IN_MCU is 10. A joint constraint that no per-field value set can express, which is why it lives here.

then.detail: the entropy-coded segment must carry an RSTn marker after every Ri MCUs, cycling 0xFFD0 to 0xFFD7

dependencies.description: A non-zero restart interval obliges the scan to contain matching restart markers - the payload is derived from Ri, and Ri is never narrowed to suit a fixed payload.
dependencies.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: Ri = 1, 2, 4 and 100 with matching markers all decode cleanly (rc=0). Ri = 2 with no markers at all gives rc=2 'Corrupt JPEG data: 21 extraneous bytes before marker 0xd9' - the scan is abandoned at the first missing restart, so most of the image is lost even though the file is accepted.

then.detail: 3 * xThumbnail * yThumbnail bytes of RGB follow, and szSection must equal 16 + 3*xThumbnail*yThumbnail

dependencies.description: A JFIF APP0 declaring a non-zero thumbnail size must carry exactly that many RGB triples - the array is derived from the two dimension bytes.
dependencies.note: The template emits the array only when BOTH xThumbnail and yThumbnail are non-zero (line 1113), so a file with one of them zero carries no array and szSection is 16.

then.detail: a complete nested JPEG datastream of szSection - 8 bytes follows, parsed recursively as a JPGFILE

dependencies.description: JFXX extension 0x10 embeds a whole JPEG file as the thumbnail.
dependencies.note: Lines 1124-1127 save JpegFileEnd, set it to FTell() + szSection - 8, parse a nested JPGFILE and restore it. The nested file must itself satisfy every rule in this document, including its own SOI and EOI, and must fit exactly in szSection - 8 bytes.

then.detail: two thumbnail dimension bytes, then a fixed 256-entry RGB palette (768 bytes), then szSection - 8 index bytes

dependencies.description: JFXX extension 0x11 carries a palettised thumbnail with a full 256-colour palette.
dependencies.note: For the segment to be self-consistent szSection - 8 must equal 2 + 768 + xThumbnail*yThumbnail - see the template quirk recorded on APP0.pixel, where the index array is sized from szSection rather than from the dimensions.

then.detail: two thumbnail dimension bytes, then xThumbnail * yThumbnail RGB triples

dependencies.description: JFXX extension 0x13 carries an uncompressed RGB thumbnail whose size is derived from its declared dimensions.

then.detail: an 8-byte TIFF header must follow: align[2] = 'II' or 'MM', tagMark = 42 in that byte order, offsetFirstIFD (normally 8)

dependencies.description: The EXIF branch commits the segment to carrying a complete, self-consistent TIFF block.
dependencies.note: Every multi-byte field in the whole TIFF block - and every offset in the IFD chain - is read in the byte order this header declares.

then.detail: when dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent <= 4 the value is stored inline and padding fills the remainder; otherwise these four bytes are an offset from the TIFF header origin

dependencies.description: Whether a directory entry's value is inline or out of line is decided entirely by its format and count.
dependencies.note: The boundary is tested at line 786 and again at line 957. Both sides matter: the inline side reaches the typed readers and the padding field, the offset side reaches the second loop at lines 961-1027 and, through it, every recursive sub-parser.

then.detail: the template emits an inline value for uLong1, sLong and sFloat only when nComponent == 1 (lines 897, 911, 915); with any other count and a length still <= 4 no field is emitted at all

dependencies.description: Three of the inline readers are guarded by an additional count test, so some legal format/count combinations produce an entry with no value field in the template's view.
dependencies.note: TEMPLATE QUIRK. dataFormat 10 (sRatio) and 12 (dFloat) have no inline reader at all, but their element widths are 8 bytes so a length <= 4 is impossible and the case never arises. For uLong1, sLong and sFloat with nComponent == 1 the length is exactly 4, so the padding field at line 922 is skipped too.

then.detail: when the thumbnail IFD's Compression tag equals 6, the thumbnail bytes are parsed as a complete nested JPEG file; for any other value they are read as opaque imageData

dependencies.description: Compression = 6 (old-style JPEG) is what turns the EXIF thumbnail into a recursively parsed JPEG stream.
dependencies.note: Lines 1200-1227. The thumbnail is located by ThumbnailOffset (0x0201) or StripOffsets (0x0111) and sized by ThumbnailLength (0x0202) or StripByteCounts (0x0117); all four must agree with where the bytes actually are. The local 'compression' is initialised to 10 at line 1200, so a thumbnail IFD with no Compression tag takes the opaque branch.

then.detail: the MakerNote branch is entered only when CameraMake starts with 'CASIO COMPUTER CO.,LTD' and CameraModel starts with 'QV-R62'; it then consumes a 6-byte header and parses a nested Casio IFD

dependencies.description: The Casio maker-note sub-parser is gated on two string comparisons against values read from earlier tags.
dependencies.note: Lines 1051-1062. CameraMake and CameraModel are filled at lines 945 and 949 from the Make (0x010f) and Model (0x0110) tags of the SAME IFD, so those two entries must appear, must have dataFormat ascString, and must carry exactly those strings - and, because they are longer than four bytes, must be stored out of line with correct offsets. This is the deepest conditional branch in the template.

then.detail: sData and oData follow; for any other storage method the entry instead carries 8 inline bytes

dependencies.description: CIFF entries are either heap-stored (size plus offset) or record-stored (eight inline bytes), never both.

then.detail: kDT_HeapTypeProperty1 and kDT_HeapTypeProperty2 make the value block a nested CIFF directory, parsed by recursing into CDIR with cDirOffset and cDirSize set from this entry

dependencies.description: Two CIFF data types turn an entry's value into a nested directory, which is the only recursion in the CIFF parser.

then.detail: every symbol in a DC table must be in the range 0..15

dependencies.description: DC Huffman tables carry magnitude categories, which cannot exceed 15.
dependencies.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: a DC table containing symbol 16 or 255 gives rc=1 'Bogus Huffman table definition' and no output; the identical table declared as an AC table (htInfo 0x10) with symbol 255 decodes normally. The class nibble therefore changes the legal symbol set.

then.detail: the 64 coefficients are read as big-endian uint16 rather than as bytes, doubling the table's contribution to szSection from 64 to 128 bytes

dependencies.description: The quantization table's element width is selected by Pq, which changes both the array type and the segment length.

then.detail: block_num must run from 1 to block_total with no gaps or duplicates across the file's APP2 segments, and every chunk must declare the same block_total

dependencies.description: A multi-segment ICC profile is reassembled by chunk index, and any inconsistency makes the whole profile be discarded.
dependencies.note: libjpeg's jpeg_read_icc_profile rejects the sequence before examining a single profile byte.

then.detail: a pad byte is present when namelen is even (the template's test is namelen % 2 != 1) and absent when it is odd

dependencies.description: Photoshop Image Resource names are padded so that the length byte plus the name occupies an even number of bytes.
dependencies.note: Line 1345. The companion rule at line 1350 pads the data: a pad byte follows when size is odd.

dependencies.description: For a three-component frame the Adobe transform code selects between raw RGB (0) and YCbCr (1); for a four-component frame it selects between CMYK (0) and YCCK (2).
dependencies.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: with no Adobe marker a 3-component frame is always assumed to be YCbCr, so transform 0 is the only way to make libjpeg decode a 3-component JPEG as raw RGB and take the null colour-conversion path. A 4-component frame with transform 1 warns 'Unknown Adobe color transform code 1' and still decodes.

then.detail: these markers are standalone in ITU-T T.81 and carry NO length field, but the template unconditionally reads a WORD szSection after every unknown marker

dependencies.description: The RSTn markers, SOI, EOI and TEM are standalone; routing them through the UNKNOWN struct appends two bytes that the format does not define.
dependencies.note: TEMPLATE LIMITATION, recorded rather than hidden. A generator emitting one of these through the UNKNOWN path produces a segment whose two 'length' bytes a decoder will read as the beginning of the next marker. Measured: an RST0 and a TEM inserted before the SOS were both tolerated by libjpeg-turbo (rc=0) because it skips standalone markers without reading a length, so the two extra bytes were then resynchronised past - but the file is not what the template thinks it is.

structure.subject: JPGFILE.SOIMarker
structure.detail: The two bytes FF D8 must be the very first bytes of the file, with nothing before them.
structure.description: A JPEG file begins with SOI and a decoder refuses anything else outright.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: four bytes prepended gives rc=1 'Not a JPEG file: starts with 0x00 0x01'. The template, by contrast, tolerates leading garbage through the 'char garbage' branch at line 1621 - a divergence a generator must resolve in the decoder's favour.
structure.generation_note: Emit FF D8 unconditionally as the first element of the file, outside the marker loop, never as one iteration of it.

structure.subject: SOFx
structure.detail: Exactly one frame header must appear, and it must precede the SOS.
structure.description: Without a frame header there is no image to decode.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo reports 'Invalid JPEG file structure: missing SOS marker' when it reaches EOI with no scan, and refuses a file with no frame header.
structure.generation_note: Emit one of SOF0, SOF1, SOF2 or SOF3 before the SOS. Emitting two frame headers is not expressible in this template, because the marker loop terminates at the first SOS.

structure.subject: SOS
structure.detail: At least one scan header must appear, after the frame header.
structure.description: The SOS is what starts the entropy-coded data; a file without one decodes nothing.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: an EOI placed before any SOS gives rc=1 'Invalid JPEG file structure: missing SOS marker'.
structure.generation_note: Emit the SOS last among the header segments; everything the scan references must already have been defined.

structure.subject: DQT
structure.detail: A DQT segment defining every table a frame component names must appear before the SOS.
structure.description: Quantization tables are mandatory and libjpeg refuses a file that references an undefined one.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: omitting the DQT gives rc=1 'Quantization table 0x00 was not defined' with no output. This is the only table segment whose absence is fatal.
structure.generation_note: Emit at least one DQT before the SOF, or at least before the SOS, defining each Tq that any COMPS.compNr names.

structure.subject: DHT
structure.detail: A DHT segment defining every table the scan references should appear before the SOS.
structure.description: The standard requires the tables; libjpeg-turbo substitutes the Annex K defaults when they are missing.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: omitting the DHT entirely gives rc=2 and a complete image, not a failure - it falls back to the standard tables. Other decoders raise 'Huffman table 0x00 was not defined' and stop.
structure.generation_note: Emit the DHT before the SOS. Omitting it occasionally is worth doing precisely because it reaches libjpeg-turbo's default-table fallback, which a conforming file never touches.

structure.subject: DQT, DHT, DRI, APPn, COM relative to SOS
structure.detail: Every table and parameter segment must precede the SOS that uses it.
structure.description: JPEG is a single-pass format: a table takes effect from the point it is defined.
structure.generation_note: Build the file as SOI, then a freely ordered and freely repeated run of APPn/COM/DQT/DHT/DRI segments, then the SOF, then the SOS. The SOF may appear anywhere before the SOS; libjpeg does not care whether tables precede or follow it, only that they precede the scan.

structure.subject: JPGFILE marker loop
structure.detail: The loop at line 1540 emits zero or more segments before the SOS and terminates at the first SOS.
structure.description: The body of a JPEG file is a repeated sequence of marker segments.
structure.output_budget: Budget the whole marker-segment run to about 96 KB of generated bytes, measured as a running total the generator increments by each segment's full size (2 marker bytes plus szSection) and checks before starting another segment. When the budget is exhausted, stop adding segments and proceed to the SOF and SOS. This is the only place total file size is controlled: no dimension, count, table size or thumbnail size is ever capped to achieve it. Note that the scan data is budgeted separately, because it is derived from the dimensions rather than chosen.
structure.generation_note: Emit SOI as a fixed head, then a repeated array of marker segments bounded by output_budget, then the SOF, the SOS, the derived scan, and EOI as a fixed tail.

structure.subject: Huffmann_Table within one DHT segment
structure.detail: One DHT segment carries one or more tables back to back; the loop at line 1418 consumes them until szSection is exhausted.
structure.description: Several Huffman tables may share a single segment.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: 1, 2, 4 and 8 tables in one DHT segment all decode (rc=0). Redefining the same htInfo overwrites the earlier table.
structure.output_budget: Budget all DHT segments together to about 16 KB. Each table costs 17 + sum(length) bytes and sum(length) may be up to 256, so one table can reach 273 bytes and the theoretical maximum for four distinct DC and four AC tables is about 2 KB. The budget bounds how many segments repeat, never the shape of any individual table - length[] is derived from the code being built, not clipped to fit.
structure.generation_note: Emit one segment holding the tables the scan needs, then optionally repeat with redefinitions while the budget allows.

structure.subject: QuanTable within one DQT segment
structure.detail: One DQT segment carries one or more tables back to back; the loop at line 1438 consumes them until szSection is exhausted.
structure.description: Several quantization tables may share a single segment.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 tables in one DQT segment all decode (rc=0).
structure.output_budget: Budget all DQT segments together to about 8 KB. A table costs 65 bytes at Pq=0 and 129 at Pq=1, so the four distinct destinations cost at most 516 bytes; the rest of the budget allows redefinitions. The 64-coefficient table size is fixed by the format and is never the thing trimmed.
structure.generation_note: Emit one segment defining each Tq the frame names, then optionally repeat.

structure.subject: DIRENTRY within one IFD
structure.detail: An IFD is a count followed by that many 12-byte entries and a next-IFD pointer; entries may point at arbitrarily large out-of-line values.
structure.description: The EXIF directory is the template's largest repeating structure.
structure.output_budget: Budget each APP1 EXIF block to about 24 KB in total, counting the 12-byte entries and every out-of-line value they point at, and stop adding entries when the running total would exceed it. A JPEG segment cannot exceed 65535 bytes in any case, so the block must also fit that hard format limit. Neither IFD.nDirEntry nor DIRENTRY.nComponent is capped to achieve this - the generator stops adding entries instead.
structure.generation_note: Emit the count, then entries while the budget allows, then the next-IFD pointer, then the out-of-line value blocks at the offsets the entries declared.

structure.subject: IFD chain
structure.detail: IFDs are chained by nextIFDoffset; the template follows exactly one link, from the main image IFD to the thumbnail IFD, and recurses separately into Exif, GPS, interoperability and Casio sub-IFDs.
structure.description: The EXIF directory structure is a shallow tree, not a flat list.
structure.output_budget: Limit the chain to the two links the template models (main and thumbnail) and sub-IFD recursion to depth 2, and count every nested IFD against the same 24 KB APP1 budget. Recursion depth is the size control here, not the entry counts.
structure.generation_note: Set nextIFDoffset to 0 to end the chain, or to a correct forward offset to open the thumbnail IFD - which is also the only route to the embedded thumbnail JPEG.

structure.subject: CifDirEntry within one CDIR
structure.detail: A CIFF directory is a heap of value blocks followed by an entry count, that many 10-byte entries, and a trailing offset.
structure.description: The Canon CIFF block in APP0 is a self-contained nested directory with its own recursion.
structure.output_budget: Budget the whole CIFF block to about 8 KB and nested CDIR recursion to depth 2. The heap region and the entry array grow together, so the generator tracks one running total covering both and stops adding entries when it would be exceeded.
structure.generation_note: Lay the block out heap-first: value blocks, then nDirEntry, then the entries, then szValues holding the offset back to nDirEntry.

structure.subject: APP12 entry chain
structure.detail: The Ducky block is a chain of tag/length/value entries terminated by a DK_End tag.
structure.description: APP12's structure is a self-terminating list rather than a counted array.
structure.output_budget: Budget the APP12 segment to about 4 KB. Because the chain is terminated by an explicit DK_End rather than by a reliable byte count (see the quirk on APP12.szSection), the generator must always close it; the budget decides how many entries precede the terminator.
structure.generation_note: Emit entries while the budget allows, then a DK_End entry, then set szSection from the total.

structure.subject: APP13 block chain
structure.detail: The Photoshop IRB section is a run of variable-length blocks consumed while remainsize > 0.
structure.description: APP13's structure is a byte-budgeted run with per-block padding rules.
structure.output_budget: Budget the APP13 segment to about 8 KB. Each block costs 4 signature bytes + 2 tag bytes + 1 namelen + the padded name + 4 size bytes + the padded data; the generator adds blocks while the total stays inside the budget and then sets szSection so that remainsize (szSection - 16) matches the blocks emitted.
structure.generation_note: Emit blocks, then compute szSection from what was emitted - never truncate a block to fit a preset length.

structure.subject: APP0 JFIF thumbnail rgb array
structure.detail: The RGB array holds exactly xThumbnail * yThumbnail triples.
structure.description: The JFIF thumbnail is a derived payload, sized entirely by two free dimension bytes.
structure.output_budget: Budget the APP0 segment to about 8 KB. When the budget is smaller than 16 + 3*x*y for the dimensions drawn, the correct response is to emit NO thumbnail - set xThumbnail and yThumbnail to 0 - not to shrink them to make a payload fit. The maximum possible is 255*255*3 = 195075 bytes, which exceeds the 65535-byte segment limit, so the dimensions must in any case satisfy 16 + 3*x*y <= 65535 for the segment to be representable at all.
structure.generation_note: Draw the dimensions freely, compute the array from them, and compute szSection from the array.

structure.subject: JPGFILE.scanData
structure.detail: The entropy-coded data must run contiguously from the end of the SOS header to the EOI, interrupted only by RSTn markers.
structure.description: Nothing may be inserted into a scan except restart markers.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: an 0xFF byte in the scan that is not followed by 0x00 or a legal RSTn is read as a marker and ends the scan - 'Unsupported marker type 0x7f' when the byte is not a marker libjpeg knows.
structure.generation_note: Emit the scan as one run; if Ri is non-zero, flush to a byte boundary and insert the RSTn marker, then continue.

structure.subject: JPGFILE.EOIMarker
structure.detail: FF D9 should terminate the entropy-coded data, and anything after it is ignored.
structure.description: The EOI closes the image, but it is not mandatory for libjpeg-turbo.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: with no EOI, rc=2 'Premature end of JPEG file' and the full image is still produced. With trailing garbage after the EOI, rc=0 and the image decodes identically.
structure.generation_note: Emit FF D9 as a fixed tail after the scan, then optionally a free trailing region (JPGFILE.unknownPadding). Omitting the EOI selects the unterminatedScanData branch, which is worth generating sometimes.

structure.subject: a second JPGFILE.SOIMarker
structure.detail: Exactly one SOI may appear in a file.
structure.description: A repeated SOI is a structural error.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: a second FF D8 anywhere after the first gives rc=1 'Invalid JPEG file structure: two SOI markers' and no output.
structure.generation_note: The template's dispatch switch has a case for M_SOI inside the marker loop, so it will happily parse several; a generator must emit exactly one. The exception is a nested JPGFILE inside a thumbnail, which is a separate datastream with its own SOI and is not part of the outer file's marker sequence.

structure.subject: JPGFILE.EOIMarker before the SOS
structure.detail: No EOI may appear before the scan.
structure.description: An early EOI ends the datastream with no image.
structure.measured_gate: libjpeg-turbo: an FF D9 inserted before the SOS gives rc=1 'Invalid JPEG file structure: missing SOS marker'.
structure.generation_note: Because the template has no M_EOI case in its dispatch switch, an EOI emitted at top level would be routed to the UNKNOWN struct and given a spurious length; a generator should simply never emit one before the scan.

structure.subject: APP0 branches
structure.detail: An APP0 segment is exactly one of: JFIF main, JFXX extension, Canon CIFF, or unrecognised.
structure.description: The four layouts are selected by the segment's opening bytes and cannot be combined.
structure.generation_note: Choose the branch first, then emit the signature that selects it, then the matching body. The same applies to APP1 (Exif / XMP / unknown), APP2 (FPXR / ICC / unknown), APP13 (Photoshop / Adobe_CM / unknown) and APP14 (Adobe / unknown).

structure.subject: DRI before SOS
structure.detail: A DRI segment takes effect only for scans that follow it.
structure.description: The restart interval is a parser state set by the segment.
structure.generation_note: Emit the DRI before the SOS if restart markers are wanted. Emitting DRI with Ri = 0 explicitly disables restarts and is legal.

structure.subject: nested JPGFILE recursion
structure.detail: A JPGFILE may contain further complete JPGFILEs: as a JFXX 0x10 thumbnail, as an EXIF thumbnail with Compression 6, and as a Casio maker-note preview.
structure.description: The format is recursive, and the template models the recursion by saving and restoring the JpegFileEnd local.
structure.output_budget: Limit nesting to depth 2 and budget each nested stream to about 16 KB, counted against the enclosing segment's own budget. Each nested stream must be a complete, independently valid JPEG obeying every rule in this document, and must fit exactly in the byte count the enclosing structure declared (szSection - 8 for JFXX 0x10, thumbLength for the EXIF thumbnail, nComponent for the Casio preview).
structure.generation_note: Generate the nested file first, then set the enclosing length field from its actual size - the classic derive-the-payload-from-nothing case, since here the length is derived from the payload rather than the reverse.

diversity_axes.why: The image width. It multiplies into the MCU count and therefore into the size of the entropy-coded segment, which is exactly the shape of the GIF mistake that cost 1.7 points: a generator tempted to keep files small will narrow this field so that a precomputed scan fits. It must not. The scan is computed from the width; the width is drawn freely. Measured legal and decodable across 1 to 65500.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Width decides how many MCU columns exist and how much of the last column is edge padding. A width that is not a multiple of 8*Hmax drives libjpeg's partial-MCU path; a width below one MCU drives the dummy-block expansion in jdinput; wide images drive the row-buffer strategy in jdmainct and different inner loops in the upsamplers and colour converters.

diversity_axes.why: The image height, with exactly the same standing as the width: it multiplies into the MCU count and the scan is derived from it. Measured legal and decodable across 1 to 65500.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Height decides the number of MCU rows, whether the final row is partial, and how many times the multi-pass buffer controller cycles. A height of 1 exercises the single-row path; a tall narrow image exercises the row-group machinery repeatedly.

diversity_axes.why: The component count. Its legal set is pinned to 1..10 by the decoder, but which of the ten a file uses is a completely free choice, and it is the single field that most reshapes the decode: 1, 3 and 4 select grayscale, YCbCr and CMYK colour handling respectively, while 2 and 5..10 select the unknown-colour-space null conversion. Emitting only 3 - the obvious 'safe' choice - would delete three whole colour pipelines.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects the colour converter (jdcolor: grayscale_convert, ycc_rgb_convert, ycck_cmyk_convert, null_convert), the upsampler configuration, and the number of component loops in the entropy decoder.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because 11 or more is refused outright ('Too many color components: N, max 10'), but 'unconstrained' here means the full legal set 1..10 must be emitted, not narrowed to the convenient values. The distinction is the same one used for GIF's DATASUBBLOCK.Size: the value is bounded by an identity, the choice within those bounds is free.

diversity_axes.why: The horizontal sampling factor. Its legal set is 1..4 and all four must be emitted: subsampling is what makes a JPEG's components have different resolutions, and it is the main reason MCUs contain more than one block per component.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects the upsampling routine - h2v1_upsample, h2v2_upsample, the fancy variants, or int_upsample for unusual ratios - and changes the block interleaving order inside decode_mcu.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because 0 and 5 give 'Bogus sampling factors'; the four legal values are all free choices, subject to the joint sum(Hi*Vi) <= 10 rule recorded in dependencies.

diversity_axes.why: The vertical sampling factor, with the same standing as COMPS.Horz.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Together with Horz it selects the upsampler and decides how many data units each component contributes to an MCU, which is the innermost loop bound of the entropy decoder.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A for the same measured reason as COMPS.Horz.

diversity_axes.why: The number of components in the scan. 1 produces a non-interleaved scan and 2..4 produce interleaved scans, and the two cases use entirely different MCU geometry and entirely different loops - so the choice reshapes the scan payload completely.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Ns == 1 selects libjpeg's non-interleaved path, where the MCU is a single data unit and the count comes from the component's own dimensions; Ns > 1 selects the interleaved path with Hi*Vi data units per component per MCU.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because 0 and 5+ are refused with 'Bogus marker length'; all four legal values are free choices.

diversity_axes.why: The restart interval. It is a count that the entropy-coded payload must agree with, so the payload is derived from it - restart markers are emitted every Ri MCUs. Measured free across the whole 16-bit span.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Ri == 0 disables the restart machinery entirely. Ri > 0 makes the entropy decoder check for a restart marker after every interval, call process_restart, reset the DC predictors and the bit buffer, and - if the marker is missing or out of sequence - enter the resynchronisation path. Ri == 1 exercises that machinery once per MCU.

diversity_axes.why: The Huffman code shape. It is not a value to be pinned to the standard Annex K tables: the code shape decides how many bits each symbol costs and therefore how large the scan is, and it selects between libjpeg's fast lookup path and its slow bit-by-bit path. The scan is derived from the table.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Codes of 8 bits or fewer are resolved by the look-ahead table in HUFF_DECODE; longer codes fall through to jpeg_huff_decode's bit-at-a-time loop. A table using only short codes never reaches the slow path; a table with 16-bit codes reaches it constantly.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because a code that overflows the code space is refused with 'Bogus Huffman table definition'. Free means: build the shape freely within the Kraft rule, do not fall back to one fixed table.

diversity_axes.why: The Huffman symbol list. Which symbols the table defines decides which symbols the scan may use, and therefore which decoder branches the scan can reach - EOB, ZRL, long zero runs, large magnitude categories.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: AC symbol 0x00 takes the EOB path, 0xF0 takes the ZRL path, and a symbol with a non-zero size nibble takes the extend-and-accumulate path. A DC symbol of category s makes the decoder read s additional raw bits and sign-extend them.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because a DC table containing a symbol above 15 is refused; within that rule the symbol choice is free.

diversity_axes.why: The table class and destination. Emitting all four destinations rather than only 0 is what lets a file use different tables for different components, which is what real encoders do and what the multi-table bookkeeping in jdhuff handles.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects which of libjpeg's eight table slots is filled and, through the class bit, whether the DC symbol range check applies.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because anything outside the eight legal values gives 'Bogus DHT index N'; all eight are free choices.

diversity_axes.why: The scan's table destination selectors decide which of the defined tables each component uses. Varying them across components is what exercises the per-component table binding in start_pass_huff_decoder.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each distinct selector causes a separate jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl call and a separate derived-table cache entry.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because an undefined or out-of-range destination raises JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE; the four legal values are free choices.

diversity_axes.why: The companion table selector, with the same standing as COMPSOS.AC.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: As for COMPSOS.AC.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A for the same reason.

diversity_axes.why: The coding process. This is the highest-leverage single choice in a JPEG file and the one a size-conscious author is most likely to fix at SOF0. Measured, all four routed values reach a real decoder, and SOF2 and SOF3 reach decoders that share almost no code with the baseline one.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: SOF0/SOF1 drive jdhuff's sequential decoder and jdcoefct's single-pass controller. SOF2 drives jdphuff, the multi-scan buffered-image controller and the coefficient-refinement logic. SOF3 drives libjpeg-turbo's lossless predictor and difference decoder, which shares no code with the DCT path at all.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because only four values reach this struct; all four are free choices and all four should be emitted.

diversity_axes.why: Sample precision. Emitting 12 alongside 8 is one of the cheapest large coverage gains available in this format, because libjpeg-turbo 3.x compiles a second, complete 12-bit instantiation of the DCT, quantization, upsampling and colour pipeline. Under SOF3 the legal set widens to 2..16 and all of it was measured to decode.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 8 and 12 select entirely separate compiled instantiations of the sample pipeline in libjpeg-turbo 3.x; under SOF3 the lossless path additionally handles 2..16.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because out-of-set values give 'Unsupported JPEG data precision N'; within the set the choice is free and both members matter.

diversity_axes.why: The Adobe colour transform. Its three values reinterpret the same component data three different ways, and for a 3-component frame it is the only way to make a decoder treat the components as raw RGB instead of YCbCr.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects jdcolor's converter: null_convert for RGB, ycc_rgb_convert for YCbCr, ycck_cmyk_convert for YCCK. Values above 2 reach the JWRN_ADOBE_XFORM warning path.

diversity_axes.why: The 64 quantization coefficients. The obvious move is to emit one standard table forever; measurement says every value from 0 to 65535 is legal, and the coefficients scale every dequantized value, so they control the numeric range that reaches the IDCT.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Large coefficients push IDCT outputs past the sample range and into the range-limiting table; all-zero coefficients produce a flat block; mixed tables exercise the per-coefficient multiply in the dequantization loop. libjpeg also chooses between its slow, fast-integer and float IDCT variants independently, and the coefficient magnitudes decide whether their results differ.

diversity_axes.why: The quantization element width. Both values are legal and they select different read loops and different table storage.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Pq=0 reads 64 bytes, Pq=1 reads 64 big-endian words; the second doubles the segment length and is forbidden in baseline files by T.81 though not by libjpeg.

diversity_axes.why: The spectral selection start, or the lossless predictor. Under SOF2 it ranges over all 64 coefficient indices and under SOF3 over the seven predictors - two completely different meanings for the same byte, both of which reach real code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Under SOF2 it partitions the coefficients across scans and selects between jdphuff's DC and AC decoders; under SOF3 it selects one of seven prediction formulas in the lossless decoder.

diversity_axes.why: The spectral selection end, free over 0..63 in a progressive frame.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Together with Ss it defines the coefficient band a progressive scan carries, which decides how many refinement passes the coefficient controller runs.

diversity_axes.why: Component identifiers. Measured completely free, duplicates included; the only requirement is that the scan names the same values. A generator tempted to hard-code 1,2,3 would never produce the Adobe convention ('R','G','B') or the duplicate-id files that real cameras occasionally emit.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives the linear search in get_sos that matches scan components to frame components, including its failure path.

diversity_axes.why: Which unmodelled marker to emit. This is the template's only route to twelve marker values that libjpeg-turbo handles specially, including the arithmetic frame headers 0xFFC9-0xFFCB, which open an entire alternative entropy decoder, and 0xFFCC (DAC) with its own validation.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0xFFC9/0xFFCA route the file into jdarith.c, a complete arithmetic decoder that shares no code with jdhuff. 0xFFCC drives get_dac and its range checks. 0xFFDC drives the DNL path. The unsupported SOF types and 0xFFDE/0xFFDF/0xFFF7 drive libjpeg's rejection paths.

diversity_axes.why: Which chunk of an ICC profile this segment carries. How many chunks a profile is split into is a free choice, and a multi-chunk profile is the only way to exercise a reader's reassembly code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg's jpeg_read_icc_profile walks every APP2 marker, validates the index sequence and concatenates the chunks; a single-chunk profile skips the concatenation loop entirely.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A because the indices must form an exact 1..block_total sequence; how many chunks there are is free.

diversity_axes.why: The chunk count for an embedded ICC profile; a free choice that the per-chunk indices must then match.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Decides how many APP2 markers the reassembly loop visits.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier A as an identity that every chunk must repeat; the number itself is free.

diversity_axes.why: The EXIF directory entry count. Every additional entry is another pass through the twelve-way dataFormat switch and another chance to hit one of the five recursion-opening tags, so capping it caps how much of the EXIF parser any file can reach.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bounds three separate loops over the directory and decides how many sub-IFD recursions a file can open.

diversity_axes.why: The element count of a directory entry's value. It decides, together with the format, whether the value is stored inline or out of line - the single most consequential branch in the TIFF entry parser - and it sizes eleven different arrays.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: length <= 4 takes the inline readers and the padding field; length > 4 takes the offset branch and the second loop, which is where every recursive sub-parser lives.

diversity_axes.why: The TIFF value type. Each of the twelve selects a different reader and a different element width; narrowing to the common few deletes the rest.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects among twelve inline readers and ten out-of-line readers, each a distinct struct declaration.

diversity_axes.why: The EXIF tag. Five values open recursive sub-parsers - the Exif sub-IFD, the GPS IFD, the interoperability IFD, the Casio maker note and an embedded preview JPEG - and two more (Make, Model) gate the maker-note branch. The enumeration is large on purpose.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives four separate switch statements in the template and, in a real EXIF reader, the per-tag interpretation table.

diversity_axes.why: The CIFF directory entry count; every entry is another pass through the property switch and another chance to open a nested directory.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Bounds the entry array and the property loop; two data types recurse into a nested CDIR.

diversity_axes.why: A dimension that sizes a payload - the JFIF RGB thumbnail array - which makes it the exact analogue of the GIF field that was wrongly narrowed. Derive the array from it; never shrink it to fit an array.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Non-zero values make the template emit the RGB array and make a JFIF-aware consumer decode a thumbnail; zero skips both.

diversity_axes.why: The other half of the same dimension pair, with the same standing.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: As for APP0.xThumbnail.

diversity_axes.why: The JFXX thumbnail encoding. One of its three values embeds a complete nested JPEG file, which is the deepest recursion the APP0 structure offers.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects between a recursive JPGFILE parse, a palettised thumbnail with a 768-byte palette, and a raw RGB thumbnail.

diversity_axes.why: The only completely unconstrained bulk payload in the format. It is the right place to vary file size and byte content freely, which is why the size budget lives on the marker loop and not on any field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Skipped by libjpeg, so it contributes no decoder branches of its own - but it lets a file's size and byte distribution vary without touching anything that is validated.

diversity_axes.why: Inter-segment filler. Emitting it deliberately reaches libjpeg's next_marker resynchronisation loop and its 'extraneous bytes' warning, which a clean file never touches.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives jdmarker's next_marker skip loop and the JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA path.
